## Verified-against-origin/master highlights

- The ordinary userspace full-apply failure remains swallowed at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:903-911`, while successful applied identity is advanced elsewhere. A tightening commit can report success while the old permit remains live; this is separate from peer equal-text retry (`#4957`) and planned-failover epoch (`#5563`).
- Flowless non-first fragments still return `NatDecision::default()` in `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/mod.rs:3906-3909`; the lower frame layer supports address-only fragment rewrites, so ordinary NAT/NPT consistency is genuinely missing rather than impossible.
- The config multi-root defect remains structural: first-root prepasses use `FindChild`, while dispatch compiles every matching root. The reproduced split-root QinQ and range-filter cases survive strict admission; the claimed `#5631` alias subtrace was independently refuted and removed.
- The fresh issue delta changed disposition, not reachability: scheduler and DHCP-relay rows are now `DUP_OPEN #5669/#5670`; inline ICMP, DNAT expansion, and raw NAT action cardinality are exact `DUP_CLOSED_REOPEN #3366/#3449/#5628`; feed and duplicate-local-address residuals reopen `#5645/#3718`.
- Web management still listens on 8080/8443 while both Go nft and Rust host-inbound service catalogs admit 80/443, and authored Junos interface names are still passed literally to `net.InterfaceByName`. These are separate availability roots.

## Findings by confidence

### High confidence, High severity

M02, M03, M09-M12, M17, M18, M23, M24, M28, M33, and M40 are directly evidenced High-severity roots. Each has a complete runtime trace and hostile refutation in its embedded source, cross-layer, and/or design-review appendix. The coordinator independently checked that all cited owner paths remain unchanged at the fresh tip.

### High confidence, Medium severity

M01, M04-M08, M13-M16, M19-M22, M25-M27, M29-M32, M34-M39, and M41-M43 are directly evidenced Medium roots. Each changes live forwarding, policy/NAT/session correctness, commit truth, HA availability, management reachability, or appliance lifecycle behavior. Exact evidence, trace, refutation, HPC check, impact, fix direction, labels, dedup note, and fresh-tip verification appear in the embedded report that owns the ID.

### Low-materiality/high-confidence survivors

The five cohort buckets aggregate 21 raw structured COHORT sections plus one raw MATERIAL section downgraded by design review, for 22 post-gate cohort mappings. They are real hardening work but do not independently cross the live-enforcement/materiality bar on the demonstrated trace. No low-confidence candidate is promoted to MATERIAL.

## 1. Stable-ID multi-root

**Verdict: APPROVE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

`ConfigTree.FindChild` returns only the first matching top-level child (`pkg/config/ast.go:129-137`). The pre- and post-expansion collectors in `zoneid.go`, `routinginstanceid.go`, and `tunnelid.go` use that first-match view, while `compiler_dispatch.go:31-57` compiles every matching root in author order. The reproduced single-root collision pairs fail strict validation, but equivalent split-root zone and tunnel pairs pass; the split VRF pair passes and the later VRF is quarantined with a warning. Runtime zone quarantine, tunnel `usedIDs`, and routing-instance collision handling prevent aliasing but do not make a green strict commit followed by object loss correct.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** collect every same-name top-level root in every stable-ID view, including node/group-expanded views, before collision admission. A shared all-root iterator is appropriate. Add single-root/split-root parity tests for frozen zone, VRF, and tunnel collisions and assert rejection before runtime quarantine/publication.

**Partition:** one umbrella issue is correct for these three collectors because the defect and admission fix are identical. Keep it separate from interface multi-root: interfaces require merge/precedence semantics, not merely a complete identity union.

## 2. Interface multi-root

**Verdict: REVISE. Severity: High. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL core.**

The material core is reachable. `compiler_interface_range.go:55-61`, `compiler_interfaces_unsupported.go:86-93`, and `compiler_interface_unit_alias.go:75-82` inspect only the first `interfaces` root; dispatch compiles every root, and `compiler_interfaces.go` replaces a whole same-named typed interface on a later pass. A later-root QinQ stanza passed strict schema/compile and retained `InnerVlanID`. A first-root range-applied input filter followed by a later explicit member passed and emitted an interface with the filter erased. XDP strips only one VLAN tag, so accepting unsupported QinQ is not harmless; filter replacement is a direct fail-open.

Z1's `#5631` subtrace is not reachable as stated. Two authored roots containing the same interface with `unit 00` and `unit 0` are rejected first by the duplicate-interface gate from `#5180`. A range-generated member can evade that pre-expansion gate, but later compilation replaces the whole interface; it does not converge both aliases in the same unit map, which is `#5631`'s root. Therefore this is not `DUP_CLOSED_REOPEN #5631`.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** build one merge-preserving effective interfaces view across all roots before range expansion, unsupported-feature validation, effective-name/alias validation, and typed lowering. Merely iterating each validator over each root is insufficient because range-generated and explicit members still require deterministic member-local merge/precedence instead of whole-object replacement. Tests must cover split-root QinQ, range/member filter retention, generated effective-name collisions, and emitted snapshot state.

**Partition:** one interface-root umbrella is acceptable if its acceptance criteria cover both validation completeness and replacement semantics. It must remain separate from stable-ID multi-root.

## 3. Cross-kind address shadow

**Verdict: APPROVE. Severity: High. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

`compiler_security_addressbook.go:286-337` stores addresses and address sets in separate maps without cross-kind uniqueness. Strict resolution and the live userspace resolver accept either kind and choose the address first. The typed policy/NAT reference retains only the name. A strict-pipeline reproduction defining both kinds under one name passed and both effective and live resolution selected only the address, silently narrowing a set-based deny.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** after effective address-book folding across roots/scopes, reject any name present in both namespaces. Tolerant load must warn and poison/quarantine the ambiguous identity rather than select one kind; runtime resolution needs a backstop. Cover every untagged policy and NAT consumer. Tagged references are a possible future model improvement, not required to close this admission defect.

**Partition:** one separate issue. Same-kind duplicates, recursive sets, missing references, and open `#4925` feed-backed NAT resolution have different state and repair boundaries.

## 4. Direct-host app/set precedence

**Verdict: APPROVE. Severity: High. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

`junos_host_deny.go:690-733` resolves an application-set before an application. Strict policy validation and live userspace lowering resolve application first, and `predefined.go` intentionally lets a user application shadow a same-named predefined set. A full strict-pipeline reproduction with user application `junos-ms-rpc` as TCP/22 passed, while direct-host projection emitted the predefined RPC TCP/UDP port-135 fragments instead of port 22. With coarse host SSH admission, the authored deny misses the intended service.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** direct-host projection must call a shared application-first resolver that returns the selected kind and expansion. Add end-to-end compiler, direct-host projection, and nft rendering tests for user-app/predefined-set shadowing.

**Ownership:** closed `#5629` covered AppID/NAT consumers, not direct-host projection, so this is not a residual under that closed root. Open `#5671` covers nil tolerant-loaded nested app-set classification; this trace has non-nil, resolvable objects and a lookup-order conflict. One separate novel issue is warranted.

## 5. Qualified next-hop preference

**Verdict: APPROVE. Severity: High. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

The compiler retains per-candidate qualified preference in `NextHopEntry`, but `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:64-90` serializes only next-hop strings and one route preference. The Go/Rust wire types have no candidate preference; Rust FIB construction creates unannotated candidates and selection hashes across all live candidates. A reproduced primary plus preference-250 qualified backup produced one snapshot route containing two indistinguishable next hops at route preference 5. FRR's correct rendering cannot repair metadata lost before AF_XDP selection.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** add a backward-compatible per-candidate effective preference to the Go/Rust wire and FIB. A plain candidate inherits route preference; a qualified candidate carries its own value. Selection finds the lowest-preference live tier and hashes only within that tier, remaining allocation-free. Old-wire candidates must decode as inheriting route preference. Test both-live, primary-dead, equal-tier ECMP, and old/new wire behavior.

**Partition:** one separate issue at the live AF_XDP publication/selection boundary. Closed `#3871` repaired compiler/FRR behavior and is not the same root.

## 6. Inline ICMP duplicate

**Verdict: REVISE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: `DUP_CLOSED_REOPEN #3366`.**

The defect is reachable: inline application-term parsing tracks duplicate ports, timeout, and ALG but overwrites repeated `icmp-type` and `icmp-code` without recording duplicate provenance. An opaque inline term with `icmp-type 8 icmp-type 3` passed strict admission and compiled to type 3 only. The direct-body duplicate path does not cover this parser.

The novelty claim is wrong. Closed `#3366` owns duplicate scalar leaves in this inline-term parser; ICMP fields are an omitted part of that exact repair. Closed `#5574` is only the separate direct-body parser.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** extend `#3366`'s value-aware `DuplicateTermLeaves` mechanism to inline `icmp-type` and `icmp-code`, preserving first normalized values, allowing only the established idempotent-repeat behavior, and rejecting conflicts before lowering. Add strict and tolerant tests plus emitted-term assertions. Reopen `#3366`; do not file a new umbrella.

## 7. IPsec selector cardinality

**Verdict: REVISE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

Z1's bracket-list trace is refuted by the real strict pipeline: schema scalar-leaf arity rejects a bracket list containing two CIDRs before compilation. The root nevertheless remains reachable through repeated sibling leaves. Each `local-ip`/`remote-ip` sibling independently passes schema and shape validation, while `compiler_ipsec.go:504-517` stores one scalar and applies last-wins behavior. A repeated hierarchical `local-ip` reproduction passed schema and compile and retained only the last prefix.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** aggregate occurrences per named selector and side before projection. For each present `local-ip` or `remote-ip`, enforce exactly one effective scalar across repeated siblings and group-expanded shapes; retain the existing requiredness contract rather than inventing list semantics. Tolerant load must warn and quarantine the malformed selector or dependent VPN, not silently choose a value. Exercise the real schema/commit path, repeated hierarchy/groups, rendering, and HA serialization.

**Ownership:** closed `#4098` owns selector syntax/injection. Closed `#5630` owns effective IKE endpoint validation. Neither owns repeated valid selector scalar loss, so the corrected finding is novel and separate, not `DUP_CLOSED_REOPEN #5630`.

## 8. DNAT expansion

**Verdict: REVISE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: `DUP_CLOSED_REOPEN #3449`.**

`compiler_nat_destination.go:275-294` expands a compact valid range into one `int` per port. Userspace NAT then allocates a map and another slice to coalesce it. Application-derived DNAT ranges take the same per-port expansion path. A strict-pipeline reproduction with 16 compact full-domain rules passed and retained 1,048,560 integers, about 8 MiB of integer payload before object/capacity overhead. There is no cumulative work budget.

The novelty claim is wrong. Closed `#3449` explicitly owns unbounded per-port DNAT snapshot expansion; its repair did not eliminate valid-range compiler/application expansion. This is an incomplete exact repair and must be `DUP_CLOSED_REOPEN #3449`.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** preserve compact intervals end to end for explicit and application-derived destination ports. If a compatibility bridge still requires slices, charge a deterministic whole-config budget before any expansion allocation. Tests must cover aggregate full-domain ranges across rules and applications. Open `#5658` is a destination-prefix floor problem, not port cardinality. Closed `#5628` concerns terminal-action handling, not this representation. Reopen `#3449`; do not file a new issue.

## 9. Next-table grammar and definedness

**Verdict: REVISE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL follow-on.**

The root is reachable. `parseNextTableInstance` cuts at the last `.inet` substring, so `blue.inetgarbage` can become `blue`; undefined canonical targets also pass strict validation and are only warned/skipped by the runtime applier. Both malformed-existing-target and well-formed-undefined-target reproductions passed schema and compile.

Z1's repair direction is not exact enough because current compatibility tests intentionally accept bare names and nonzero indexes, while the typed/runtime model retains only an instance name. Validation after lossy normalization cannot distinguish a bare dotted instance from a malformed suffix, and cannot enforce family/index semantics.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** validate the raw token before projection. First allow an exact bare token only when it names a defined routing instance. Otherwise require an exact terminal supported table form and extract its full dotted instance without substring matching. Because the backend has no table-index dimension, accept only representable index/family semantics (normally `.inet.0`/`.inet6.0`) and require suffix family to match the route family; update the current nonzero-index compatibility test accordingly. Then require the canonical target to exist. Tolerant load warns and omits the route, with the runtime skip retained as defense in depth.

**Partition:** grammar and definedness belong in one issue because both must operate on the same raw reference before its identity is erased. Closed `#5632` owns first-versus-last truncation of valid dotted names, not malformed suffix admission or dangling references; `#5633` owns contradictory duplicate routes.

## 10. Chassis identity zero alias

**Verdict: APPROVE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

`schema_chassis.go:181-199` leaves redundancy-group and nested node keys unvalidated. `compiler_system.go:1874-1909` initializes IDs to zero and leaves them there when `Atoi` fails; strict chassis validation then sees valid group 0/node 0. A full strict-pipeline reproduction of `redundancy-group bogus node typo priority 200` passed and emitted RG0/node0 priority 200. Cluster state is keyed by those effective integers, so malformed and legitimate identities alias.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** apply canonical decimal key validation for RG 0..255 and node 0..1 before conversion, and make conversion failure explicit rather than default-zero. Keep an effective-identity uniqueness/provenance backstop for aliases across roots/forms. Tolerant load warns and skips/quarantines malformed identity state. Test flat/hierarchical, nonnumeric, signed, leading-zero/noncanonical, out-of-range, and duplicate-effective forms.

**Partition:** one separate novel issue. Closed `#4434` owns numeric bounds after successful parsing and cannot recover erased parse provenance.

## 11. GARP work budget

**Verdict: APPROVE. Severity: Medium. Confidence: High. Owner: NOVEL.**

The schema enforces only minimum 1 despite documenting Junos 1..16. The compiler retains any architecture-sized positive value. ARP/NA burst helpers open raw sockets and run `count-1` delayed sends; VRRP and direct HA modes invoke them per VIP. A strict-pipeline reproduction accepted `MaxInt64`. Existing cancellation predicates stop work after ownership loss, not while ownership remains valid.

**Exact root/fix boundary:** clamp at the runtime burst helpers before socket/goroutine fanout so tolerant or persisted state is bounded, then make strict schema/semantic admission use the same maximum, naturally 16, with tolerant warn-and-clamp behavior. Test max, max+1, and huge values without requiring raw-socket stress. An aggregate per-interface scheduler is useful defense in depth but is not required to close this per-VIP count root.

**Partition:** one separate novel issue. Open `#5087` is day-2 count reconciliation; closed `#2867`/`#2898` are cancellation; open `#5090` is VRRP address-count wire width.

## Fresh issue dispositions

- `#5671` is open and newly present. It owns nil tolerant-loaded nested app-set classification, not direct-host application-versus-set precedence.

- Focused Rust selector test `select_route_next_hop_evaluates_liveness_once_per_candidate`: PASS.

- No raw-socket GARP stress was run; source-to-runtime fanout and strict acceptance were sufficient and avoided side effects.

## Cleanup

No source change was made. Disposable overlay tests, Cargo target output, logs, and temporary issue-query output were removed. The assigned review worktree was clean before removal; this report is the sole retained RZ1 output.

## Z2-F01: ordinary full apply failure

**Decision: REVISE. Final gate: MATERIAL, High, new root.**

### Reachability evidence

The central claim is correct on current `origin/master`:

1. `commitAndApply` promotes and persists the candidate before runtime actuation (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:284-299`). `applyAndSyncCommitted` then treats the return from `applyConfigLocked` as the commit result (`:322-354`).
2. `applyDataplaneAndHACore` has a named return `err`, but the dataplane block declares a second block-local `var err error` (`:807,903`). A non-protocol `d.dp.ApplyConfig` failure is recorded and then lost at `:904-911`. Only `compileErrorMustAbortApply` sentinels return immediately.
3. The final tail join contains networkd, DHCP, nft, IPsec, and interface errors, but not that dataplane error (`:2085-2092`). With a clean tail and invalidation, local commit and peer `SyncApply` can therefore return success.
4. Ordinary pre-ACK failures are reachable in the manager: snapshot build (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_compile.go:199-201`), bootstrap/process setup (`:291-302`), and `apply_snapshot` marshal/size/dial/write/decode/NACK (`:321-325`; `process_control.go:80-143`). They are not required-protocol sentinels.
5. On those paths, the candidate is not assigned to `m.lastSnapshot`; assignment occurs only after a successful full request (`manager_compile.go:323-327`). `syncSnapshotLocked` can retry only an already-retained newer `lastSnapshot` (`process_status.go:11-39,162-166`). It cannot reconstruct the discarded active config.
6. `/health` remains healthy after any prior compile success because only `!EverSucceeded && FailureCount > 0` returns 503 (`pkg/api/health.go:19-39`). `TakeoverReady` checks process, capabilities, arm state, mode, XSK/bindings, and session-mirror health, but no active-config/applied-config identity (`manager_ha.go:279-313`).

Concrete trace: C0 is acknowledged and permits a flow. A valid C1 tightens it to deny. The store promotes C1. A true pre-apply helper NACK, build failure, dial failure, or oversize rejection leaves C0 in `lastSnapshot`; the shadowed error lets the apply return nil; new flows still use C0; no full-snapshot retry owner exists; and an HA node can remain locally takeover-ready on C0.

### Refutation

- Previous-good retention is not fail-closed relative to a tightening; it preserves C0's permit.
- Session invalidation does not repair new-flow policy evaluation.
- `recordCompileFailure` is observability, not desired-state ownership.
- A post-apply ACK loss may mean C1 is already live, but that ambiguity does not refute the true NACK/build/dial cases. It strengthens the need for an acknowledged identity rather than treating every error as proof of old state.
- #4959 and #5485 own pre-ACK classifier-map/XDP-attachment side effects; they do not own this swallowed result, missing desired candidate, or false commit success.

### Severity and corrected fix boundary

High is justified without relying on HA: a successful tightening commit can indefinitely enforce an older permit. HA increases blast radius but is not required for severity.

The issue should own:

1. Eliminate the shadowed error and return/join every ordinary full `ApplyConfig` failure.
2. Retain daemon-level desired full-config identity/debt and retry the active config until a helper ACK or a proven status catch-up.
3. Record a local acknowledged full-config identity and make local userspace takeover readiness fail while active and applied identities differ.
4. Cover true NACK, build failure, and applied-but-ACK-lost outcomes separately.

Do **not** absorb the whole cluster config-epoch protocol into this issue. Open #4957 owns equal-active-text retry after a promoted-but-unapplied peer config; open #5563 owns planned-failover comparison of authoritative and peer-applied config epochs. They consume truthful local applied identity, while Z2-F01 is the missing producer. Link those issues, but leave their connection/high-water protocol changes in their existing owners.

## #5642 issue boundaries

### Boundary A: D-A6-F2 / Z2-F02

**Decision: APPROVE. Final gate: MATERIAL, High.**

`PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` clones `m.lastSnapshot`, replaces only config metadata and routes, then ACK-promotes the clone as the new full applied baseline (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go:146-196`). It has no proof that the cloned sections were built from the supplied config. After the swallowed C1 full-apply error, the #5642 caller runs unconditionally (`daemon_apply.go:759-771`), so it can clone C0 policy/NAT/interfaces, stamp C1, rebuild C1-era routes, and mark the hybrid applied.

This survives both failure interpretations:

- A true pre-apply failure publishes C0 policy plus post-rule C1 routes.
- An applied-but-ACK-lost full request can first install C1, after which the second request replays C0 policy/NAT over it.

The successful partial ACK advances `lastSnapshot`, `publishedSnapshot`, hash, plan key, and applied bookkeeping. Status sees convergence and cannot infer mixed provenance. High is correct because the hybrid can restore a revoked permit under an applied record labeled C1.

This is distinct from Z2-F01. Returning the first error can prevent this specific caller invocation if done immediately, but it does not establish the manager API invariant and does not protect other partial callers after an active/applied mismatch. Boundary A must require a positively acknowledged same-config full baseline or eliminate the second publication by ordering route-rule reconciliation before one complete snapshot.

No prior owner collapses it: #4959/#5485 concern candidate side effects before failed full publication; #5562 is Rust internal multi-ArcSwap publication; closed #5642 owns the deterministic no-fault stale-route path, not a positively acknowledged mixed Go snapshot.

### Boundary B: D-A6-F3 / Z2-F03

**Decision: APPROVE. Final gate: MATERIAL, Medium.**

`reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` is void and only logs both load-bearing failures (`daemon_apply.go:1478-1508`). A failed route publish installs no new `lastSnapshot`, so manager status has no desired route generation to retry. A failed `BumpFIBGeneration` is explicitly unconfirmed by contract (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_generation.go:40-55`), yet this caller retains no pending bit.

The apparent status-loop escape does not heal the bump leg. `BumpFIBGeneration` mutates `lastSnapshot.Generation`, but `syncSnapshotLocked` content-hash dedup excludes generation/FIB generation and can merely advance `publishedSnapshot` without sending the missing helper invalidation (`process_status.go:73-82`). The ip-monitoring actuator demonstrates the required design: it returns false, preserves dirty state, and retains `pendingFIBBump` until ACK (`daemon_ipmon.go:314-346`).

Publish and bump failures belong in one issue, not two. They are consecutive stages of one config-driven route-reconciliation transaction, share the same daemon owner, and have one completion predicate: kernel rule state, helper route snapshot, and cached-flow invalidation are all acknowledged. A bounded stage record keyed by config identity and route hash can retry publish, then bump, without another commit.

Closed #3757 is not an exact duplicate. It owns the ip-monitoring engine's dirty lifecycle and was fixed there; the new #5642 config-apply caller bypasses that owner. Closed #3731/#5118 own kernel RuleAdd/RuleDel error propagation, not helper route/FIB acknowledgement after a successful kernel change.

### D-A7-F01 umbrella

**Decision: REJECT as an independent issue.**

D-A7-F01 is useful corroboration but is compound. Its stale-baseline/hybrid leg is Boundary A; its route-publish and bump-error legs are Boundary B; its claim that the pipeline continues after a full error depends on Z2-F01. No single fix stated by D-A7 closes all three owners. Filing it would duplicate two #5642 issues and obscure the separate full-apply debt.

## Composite feed readiness

**D-A6-F1 / A9-D01 decision: APPROVE the DUP classification. Reopen #5645/M38; do not file a new issue.**

The residual is real. `SnapshotForBindings` skips missing/unready members but publishes the binding whenever the flattened union is nonempty (`pkg/feeds/feeds.go:457-501`). Thus one ready feed masks one never-ready feed. If every feed is omitted but the same binding name exists in the static address book, `buildAddressBookTableWithFeeds` still creates that static name/ID (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go:161-224`), and representability no longer carries any missing-feed taint. A deny then enforces only the static subset.

It nevertheless passes the strict duplicate gate against M38/#5645:

| Dimension | #5645/M38 | Composite/static residual | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Root | First-success readiness is not preserved into policy publication. | Readiness is reduced to any nonempty constituent or erased by static merge. | Same completeness root. |
| State owner | `feeds.Manager` plus the binding overlay handoff. | Same manager/handoff; static alias exposes why omission alone is lossy. | Same owner boundary. |
| Impact | Feed-backed deny under-matches/fails open. | Deny enforces a partial ready/static subset and fails open. | Same authorization class. |
| Remedy | Keep an unresolved security-bearing feed from becoming a valid matcher; retain/hold a complete generation or carry explicit unresolved state. | Require all constituents ready and preserve unresolved taint through static merge. | Same readiness barrier, broader acceptance matrix. |

The original M38 fix direction was broader than the merged `len(merged)==0` implementation: it required unresolved/ready state and holding or rejecting an incomplete policy generation. That intended boundary covers the static alias even though the chosen omission encoding cannot. Add ready+unready, unknown+ready, hold-expired+ready, and static+unready tests to #5645. #5646 remains separate desired/applied callback acknowledgement debt.

## Seven corroborated roots

### Z2-F04: stale binding retirement

**Decision: APPROVE. MATERIAL, Medium.**

Both bootstrap and live status paths ignore stale `userspace_bindings` zeroing errors and immediately discard the only index inventory (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/maps_sync.go:178-185,760-768`). The watchdog iterates only helper-expected bindings and repairs missing expected rows; it never enumerates extra READY rows (`:1181-1318`). Live status can then re-enable `userspace_ctrl` (`:784-789`). A worker-count/plan/alias change can therefore leave a retired queue pointing at a dead or reused XSK slot indefinitely.

Refutation: helper teardown does not mutate this Go-owned map; heartbeat expiry only changes the drop reason; valid-key array updates can fail and the code has no recovery even if the failure is transient. #5486 owns failure to disable ctrl before teardown, and #4894 owns queue-index alias arithmetic. Neither repairs lost stale-row inventory. Medium is proportionate: persistent per-binding outage, not a demonstrated broad policy bypass.

### Z2-F05: session-pair linearizability

**Decision: APPROVE. MATERIAL, Medium.**

`syncSessionRequestsLocked` drops `m.mu` once but calls `requestSessionSync` for each request; that callee acquires and releases `sessionMu` per fresh connection (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:1397-1422`; `process_control.go:155-185`). Rust synthesizes a reverse entry from a forward upsert, a forward delete removes both, and an explicit `is_reverse` upsert synthesizes no forward (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/ha.rs:277-309,421-515`).

Exact harmful order: forward upsert ACK; a delete writer acquires `sessionMu` and removes the pair; any companion delete it also sends can complete; then the original pair writer reacquires `sessionMu` and sends its prebuilt explicit reverse. The delete has returned while a reverse-only entry and, when locally eligible, its live session-map redirect are recreated. The policy invalidation path makes the race especially concrete because it enumerates forward entries only and deletes reverse and forward batches as separate calls (`pkg/daemon/daemon_policy_invalidate.go:300-329`; `pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:400-425`).

Refutation: Rust's single-threaded listener preserves the harmful order; there is no tombstone; generation guards compare existing same-key entries and cannot reject an upsert after deletion. #5274's config epoch does not make a same-epoch pair atomic, and #5380's dial/latency fix does not serialize it. Holding the existing `sessionMu` once around the logical pair is a distinct bounded fix. Medium is appropriate for a narrow race that can retain stale authorization.

### Z2-F06: zoned/unzoned duplicate local address

**Decision: REVISE from MATERIAL-new to DUP of closed #3718. The High trace itself is valid.**

Current code proves the trace: the unzoned builder subtracts every address present in any zoned view (`zones_host_inbound.go:353-393`); strict duplicate validation skips an owner with no zone (`pkg/config/dup_host_local_address.go:321-330`); and nft zone rules are destination-only and precede the unzoned drop (`pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:667-679,917-967`). A packet entering the unzoned interface can therefore match the zoned address's SSH accept.

But #3718 already owns the same four-part boundary: destination-only host-inbound rules, duplicate firewall-local address ownership, management-plane wrong-policy impact, and reject/quarantine-or-ingress-scope remediation. Its merged validator covered zoned-vs-zoned claims and missed zoned-vs-unzoned. The new trigger is an incomplete acceptance case, exactly like the feed residual. Reopen #3718 with zoned/unzoned static and learned IPv4/IPv6 cases; do not file Z2-F06 separately.

### Z2-F07: base/unit-0 host-inbound alias

**Decision: APPROVE. MATERIAL, Medium.**

A unit zone reference also assigns the base name to the zone (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones.go:43-83`). The snapshot builder emits both base and unit records, and ordinary unit 0 resolves both to one Linux netdev (`interfaces.go:164-300,399-428`). Only the exact unit receives its override. Host-inbound grouping places the same live address in the zone-default and override signatures (`zones_host_inbound.go:188-209`), sorts the default signature first (`:279-308`), and nft emits its catch-all drop before the later override accept.

Refutation: configured-only startup can avoid the alias, but the live netdev address makes it deterministic after realization; dedup is per signature, not across signatures; the authored config has one address owner, so #3718's strict duplicate validator cannot see the synthetic base. #5489 concerns a losing zone's override union, and #3362 is the feature antecedent. Neither normalizes base/unit-0 identity. Medium is correct for deterministic host-service outage/parity failure.

### Z2-F08: RG reconcile outlives shutdown

**Decision: APPROVE. MATERIAL, High.**

`Run` starts `reconcileRGStateLoop(ctx)` outside its wait group (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:641-645`). Shutdown cancels and waits only that group before clearing HA state and direct VIPs (`:819-850,916-950`). An in-flight pass checks no context, uses `context.Background()` for `SetRGActive`, and can reconcile direct ownership after the shutdown clear (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:494-510,555-735`). Normal direct ownership is serialized by `directVIPMu`, but shutdown calls bare `directRemoveVIPs`, bypassing the owner state machine (`daemon_ha_vip.go:162-203`).

Refutation: cancellation stops the next loop iteration, not a pass already entered; idempotence does not help when teardown requests false/remove and the late pass requests true/add; `cluster.Stop` occurs after direct removal and cannot establish a join. A late add can leave a host VIP after daemon exit even if dataplane teardown later disables transit. #5308 covered two different unjoined loops, and #5082/#5482 own VRRP-instance actuation, not direct-mode daemon shutdown. High is justified by duplicate VIP/ownership and split-forwarding risk during normal stop/restart.

### Z2-F09: unreadable kernel journal

**Decision: APPROVE. MATERIAL, High.**

`holdSecondaryIfKernelCandidateArmed` maps every `IsArmed` read/parse error to no hold (`pkg/daemon/kernel_selfrecover.go:38-50`) before `cluster.UpdateConfig` runs the first election (`daemon_run.go:1582-1603`). `loadKernelJournal` propagates non-ENOENT read and JSON errors, and both `IsArmed` and `Promote` return them (`pkg/upgrade/kernel_run.go:20-34,619-627,357-362`). The CLI exits 1, but `xpf-kernel-promote` maps that to exit 0 without reboot; systemd `OnFailure` therefore does not run (`cmd/xpfd/upgrade_kernel.go:115-127`; script lines 34-58; service lines 8-29).

Refutation: missing journal is a safe `Init` state, but permission/I/O/corruption is a distinct unknown state; BootNext fallback helps only after a later reboot; a persistent error across daemon startup and promotion leaves an unverified candidate election-eligible indefinitely. Even a transient startup-only error creates an election window before successful promotion. #4872 owns different ambiguous observations and destructive cleanup; #5275 owns dataplane arm failure. High is appropriate because the failed safety gate can let an unverified kernel preempt a healthy peer.

### Z2-F10: VRF setup false success

**Decision: APPROVE. MATERIAL, Medium.**

For an existing desired VRF with the right table, `reconcileVRFs` logs `LinkSetUp` failure, appends the VRF to `newTracked`, and returns no error for that branch (`pkg/routing/vrf.go:228-236`). Creation does treat the same setup failure as an error (`:329-350`), proving setup is part of realization. The daemon separately logs and discards all `ReconcileVRFs` and `BindInterfaceToVRF` errors, publishes management membership from `IsManagedVRF`, applies management routes, and returns nil (`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:1619-1733`). No periodic VRF reconciler owns retry.

Refutation: retaining a partially created/adopted object in the managed set is correct ownership, but `managed` is not `realized/up`; another commit may retry but does not make the current result truthful or autonomous. Closed #5310 fixed the later tunnel/XFRM/bond `applyInterfaceReconcile` phase. It neither changes `vrfManager` nor the earlier daemon phase, so this is a distinct transaction owner. Medium is proportionate for tenant/management blackhole and false convergence.

## Final recommended issue split

File these nine issues:

1. **High:** ordinary full userspace apply error is swallowed; desired full-config debt and local applied identity are absent (Z2-F01, revised boundary).
2. **High:** route-only publication accepts a baseline from a different/unacknowledged full config and ACKs a hybrid (Z2-F02).
3. **High:** RG reconciliation is not quiesced before HA/direct-VIP shutdown (Z2-F08).
4. **High:** unreadable kernel-upgrade journal bypasses candidate election hold and promotion recovery (Z2-F09).
5. **Medium:** #5642 route publication and FIB invalidation lack one staged completion-debt owner (Z2-F03).
6. **Medium:** failed stale binding clears lose retry inventory (Z2-F04).
7. **Medium:** forward/reverse session-pair transmission is not linearizable against deletes (Z2-F05).
8. **Medium:** base and unit-0 snapshots emit one live address under conflicting host-inbound signatures (Z2-F07).
9. **Medium:** VRF setup/bind failures do not reach commit truth or retry ownership (Z2-F10).

Reopen, do not file:

- **#5645/M38:** all-constituent readiness plus static-alias taint acceptance cases.
- **#3718:** zoned/unzoned duplicate firewall-local address acceptance cases.

Do not file D-A7-F01. Keep #4957, #5563, #5646, #3757, #5310, and the other adjacent owners separate as described above.

## 1. Zeroize custom-parent ownership

**Decision:** APPROVE and merge A8-b01-F1 with A8-b02-F002. **Severity:** High. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; `#5278` owns gRPC principal authorization, while closed `#5280/#4576/#5186/#5197/#5475/#5509` own under-deletion, omitted artifacts, or durability, not collateral deletion.

**Adjudication:** `cmd/xpfd/main.go:332` accepts an arbitrary `-config` file path. `configstore.New` places `.configdb` and `.config.journal` beside it without requiring an exclusive parent (`pkg/configstore/store.go:203-226`), and the custom-root regression explicitly treats `/srv/xpf/site.conf` as supported (`pkg/grpcapi/zeroize_configured_root_5280_test.go:13-69`). `zeroizeConfigRoot` promotes that file's parent to the wipe root (`pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_system_action.go:87-109`). The wipe recursively removes `<parent>/tls` and unlinks every sibling `*.conf`, `rollback*`, `.config.journal*`, and generic fsatomic temp match (`pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_zeroize.go:107-153`). The actual generated API TLS owner remains fixed under `/etc/xpf/tls` (`pkg/api/server.go:653-671`), so a custom parent's `tls/` is not proven XPF-owned. The existing bystander test covers only extensionless `node-id` and therefore misses the broad predicates.

This is reachable through a supported startup contract, not an attacker-only path. An authorized factory reset of a shared-parent custom configuration can durably remove unrelated service or system configuration and then stop the daemon. Authorization does not grant ownership of unrelated files. High is justified by irreversible cross-service data loss and possible loss of host management/network service.

**Exact issue boundary:** destructive ownership/provenance for the configured config parent: exact primary config, exact numbered rollback/rescue/journal artifacts, `.configdb`, XPF-owned temp names, and the real TLS owner. Do not absorb gRPC RBAC or prior secret-retention issues.

**Required tests:** hostile default and custom roots containing genuine XPF artifacts plus unrelated `other.conf`, `rollback-operator`, `.other.conf.tmp-*`, and `tls/foreign.key`; assert all XPF secret generations are erased and every bystander survives. Cover config symlinks and shared parents. If the chosen design requires an exclusive root, add startup rejection and durable ownership-marker tests instead of wildcard-delete tests.

## 2. MonitorInterface status multiplication

**Decision:** REVISE, retaining a MATERIAL issue. **Severity:** Medium. **Novelty:** new; closed `#3970` fixed another periodic consumer, `#5497` bounds proxy hops, and `#5278` is authorization.

**Adjudication:** summary mode recomputes all names and calls `ReadSnapshot` once per interface every second (`pkg/grpcapi/server_diag_monitor.go:478-555`). Every `ReadSnapshot` invokes its status reader (`pkg/monitoriface/monitor.go:481-523`). The production reader reaches `userspace.Manager.Status`, which holds `m.mu` across a live main-control-socket `status` round trip (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_status.go:31-52`), in addition to the mandatory one-per-second status loop (`process_status.go:134-152`). `CachedStatus` explicitly records that redundant 1 Hz status requests starve session-install progress during bulk sync (`manager_status.go:55-68`). There is no per-frame cache, broadcaster, or aggregate stream admission bound, so cost is O(N*S) live status requests per second.

The source report overstates one detail: session-sync wire I/O now uses a dedicated socket and `sessionMu` (`process_control.go:146-184`). The retained impact is main control-socket saturation and prolonged `m.mu` ownership, which delays snapshots/status operations and acquisition/preparation around session-sync and HA work; it is not a claim that session payload bytes share the same socket. A single normal multi-interface stream already violates the documented status budget, so materiality does not depend on hostile stream counts.

**Exact issue boundary:** one immutable userspace status snapshot per rendered frame, preferably the manager's mandatory 1 Hz cache, plus an aggregate stream/broadcast policy if multiple clients are supported. Keep dedicated-session-socket architecture and cancellation/proxy issues separate.

**Required tests:** a counting status reader with N interfaces must observe at most one status acquisition per frame; S concurrent summary streams must remain bounded by the documented shared-refresh policy. Cover single-interface mode, initial cache miss, helper error/last-good behavior, cancellation, and an integration fake that blocks `Status` and proves manager work is not multiplied N times.

## 3. gRPC session full-walk admission

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new. Closed `#5433` owns the REST limiter; cancellation debt has a separate prior owner; `#4886` is filtered-clear/show memory, not gRPC admission.

**Adjudication:** filtered cursor pages recompute exact totals by fully iterating v4 and v6 maps (`pkg/grpcapi/server_sessions.go:248-288`), including on continuation pages. Legacy list, session summary, and zone-pair summary also perform complete walks (`:624-715,718-805,856-969`). These RPCs are available on the primary listener and explicitly admitted on the authenticated fabric listener (`pkg/grpcapi/server.go:604-628`). Page-size caps bound response rows, not scan work. In contrast, REST has one fail-fast four-slot limiter shared across its list and aggregation handlers (`pkg/api/sessions.go:24-60`) because multi-million-entry scans contend with live session-table work. No equivalent gRPC aggregate bound exists.

**Exact issue boundary:** one shared gRPC admission owner covering legacy list, filtered exact-total scans, session summary, zone-pair summary, and the local leg of peer fanout. Decide explicitly whether filtered `Total` is optional, approximate, cached with a freshness contract, or capped. Do not merge request cancellation into this issue.

**Required tests:** a blocking fake across mixed RPC methods; cap+1 returns `ResourceExhausted`; slots release on success, iterator error, cancellation, and panic-safe paths; peer-forwarded local work participates in the same cap; filtered multipage requests have a bounded number of full scans.

## 4. DDNS identical wire-RR co-ownership

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; `#3738/#3739` protect opposite-family or different co-resident values, and `#4423` only made same-FQDN ordering deterministic.

**Adjudication:** independent interface/unit scopes can target the same provider, FQDN, family, and observed address (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:277-332`). Durable ownership remains scope-keyed (`pkg/ddns/state.go:131-175`), although DNS represents identical RDATA as one effective wire member. On definitive address loss, the departing scope directly withdraws its exact value (`pkg/ddns/surface_a.go:1005-1048`); on renumber, its previous value is replaced. The only sibling guard skips same-family records (`:1563-1588`). The surviving scope still has settled local ownership and skips reassertion until its refresh floor (`:1067-1100`). Check-IP scopes behind the same public NAT make identical observations routine.

Pass 2's provider-aware adopt guard (`surface_a.go:830-895`) correctly protects a removed stale scope when a configured same-provider scope still owns the exact tuple. Therefore the issue is specifically configured-scope loss/renumber, not config-removal cleanup.

**Exact issue boundary:** canonical wire identity `{backend endpoint/fingerprint, canonical FQDN, RR type, RDATA}` needs shared-claim accounting, or commit must reject unsupported shared claims. Delete/replace an old value only after proving no admitted scope still desires it.

**Required tests:** same-address/same-name claims across two scopes for loss and X-to-Y renumber, v4/v6, restart, per-RG writer ownership, and Cloudflare/Route53/RFC2136 value-specific backends. Include config removal as a negative control that preserves the existing Pass 2 adoption behavior.

## 5. DDNS force excludes Surface B

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; closed `#3276` introduced the command but does not own this incomplete Surface B execution.

**Adjudication:** CLI and command-tree contracts state that `update` reasserts every record owned by the node (`pkg/cli/cli_request_system.go:182-205`; `pkg/cmdtree/tree.go:996-999`). The daemon arms a force latch only on Surface A, nudges both loops, and reports that all records were forced (`pkg/daemon/daemon_ddns_surface_a.go:769-807`). Surface B has no force state; unchanged settled ownership is marked seen and no provider call occurs (`pkg/ddns/manager.go:964-980`). Thus an out-of-band deleted/corrupted DHCP forward or PTR record remains missing after the documented recovery command while success is reported.

**Exact issue boundary:** one-pass force semantics from operator command through the Surface B manager. `check` must keep changed-only behavior. Force remains subject to the existing HA/RG writer gate, provider deadlines, and error truthfulness.

**Required tests:** settled v4/v6 forward and PTR records with an externally absent backend value; `update` performs idempotent upserts while `check` does not. Cover active, standby, partial-RG ownership, provider errors, one-shot latch consumption, and truthful daemon/CLI result text.

## 6. DHCPv6 DUID continuity

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; closed `#2994` is renew/rebind IA state and the `#4909` cohort is DUID persistence failure, not acquisition/renew identity mismatch.

**Adjudication:** bare `family inet6 dhcpv6` creates a `ClientSpec` with default `DUIDType: duid-ll` but nil `V6` options (`pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp.go:47-66`). Acquisition's modifier builder returns early on nil options before calling `getDUID` (`pkg/dhcp/dhcp.go:1675-1685`), so the pinned DHCP library's `NewSolicit` inserts a generated DUID-LLT. Renew/rebind uses `buildDHCPv6RenewModifiers`, which obtains the persistent DUID-LL even when options are nil (`:1647-1659`). The Client Identifier therefore changes inside one lease lifecycle, defeating server binding identity and causing renew/rebind failure or reacquisition churn.

**Exact issue boundary:** one persistent client identity across SOLICIT/REQUEST/RENEW/REBIND/reacquire for every option shape. DUID acquisition must be independent of optional IA/ORO configuration, and identity-generation/persistence errors must not be silently omitted.

**Required tests:** capture Client-ID bytes and DUID type for bare-config acquisition, renew, and rebind; assert equality across restart and stable IAID. Repeat for configured DUID-LL and DUID-LLT, stateless behavior as applicable, and persistence/generation failures.

## 7. In-process CLI syslog overwrite

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; closed `#5581` is unknown-token fail-closed validation, not a second runtime owner overwriting a valid transport.

**Adjudication:** production wires the interactive CLI to daemon `commitAndApply` and the daemon's shared event reader (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:665-696`). The daemon apply installs source-bound UDP/TCP/TLS clients with facility and transport preserved (`pkg/daemon/daemon_system.go:99-178`; call at `daemon_apply.go:1901-1904`). After that call returns, every successful comment, confirmed, or bare CLI commit calls `reloadSyslog` (`pkg/cli/cli_config.go:177-293`). That helper rebuilds all streams with `NewSyslogClient`, which is hard-coded UDP and omits source address, facility, and transport (`pkg/cli/apply.go:53-85`; `pkg/logging/syslog.go:168-176`). `ReplaceSyslogClients` then closes the correctly configured set (`pkg/logging/ringbuf.go:388-396`). A valid TLS/TCP audit stream is therefore silently downgraded or blackholed after a routine local commit.

**Exact issue boundary:** one owner for production syslog reconciliation. Prefer daemon-only client replacement for in-process CLI commits; if standalone CLI still needs local construction, use the exact shared builder and distinguish its lifecycle explicitly. Zone-name refresh may remain shared.

**Required tests:** production-wired bare/comment/confirmed commits with an instrumented EventReader and TCP/TLS/source/facility config; assert the daemon-installed set remains exact and old connections close only once. Cover standalone CLI fallback and prove REST/gRPC commits are unaffected.

## 8. Apt URL release stamping

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** High. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; prior publish TOCTOU/signature owners concern post-gate byte identity, not generation-time shell interpretation.

**Adjudication:** the documented release runbook takes `XPF_APT_BASE_URL`, stamps `install.sh`, then signs the stamped bytes (`docs/distribution.md:55-89`). `stamp_installer` requires only a nonempty value and performs literal token replacement (`scripts/dist/publish.py:182-240`) into a single-quoted shell assignment (`scripts/dist/install.sh:40-48`). The publish gate verifies placeholder removal and the signature but never validates URL syntax or parses the generated shell (`publish.py:488-535`). A syntactically valid HTTPS path may contain an apostrophe. The hermetic review probe stamped such a path successfully, after which `dash -n` returned 2. The signature would authenticate the malformed executable text rather than constrain it.

This is a supported release input and prescribed sign order. The repository also treats hosting configuration and signing identity as separate release decisions. The issue therefore crosses a lower-trust configuration value into signed root shell syntax and can break every new Tier-A install; High is retained without relying on an executable demonstration.

**Exact issue boundary:** structured validation and shell-safe serialization of release values before signing, plus a gate over the complete stamped script. Define the supported URL policy (HTTPS, nonempty host, path/port rules, no userinfo/fragment/control ambiguity) rather than relying only on quoting.

**Required tests:** ordinary HTTPS host/path/port round trips as one scalar; quote, newline/control, userinfo, fragment, unsupported scheme, and marker-like values fail or serialize safely; run `dash -n` and shellcheck on every stamped fixture; dry-run must emit the exact intended deb822 URI without host mutation.

## 9. Systemd percent-expanded version path

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; kernel/GRUB segment owners have different sinks.

**Adjudication:** `ValidateVersionSegment` accepts every ASCII graphic except the specifically rejected path/control classes, including `%` (`pkg/upgrade/version.go:8-59`). `writeUnitDropin` inserts the resulting concrete path raw into `ExecStartPre` and `ExecStart` (`pkg/upgrade/flip.go:98-111`). Systemd expands percent specifiers in command lines. The hermetic `systemd-analyze verify` probe transformed a path containing `%n` into one containing the unit name and rejected the nonexistent expanded executable.

The producer is supported: `Makefile:8-11` embeds raw `git describe --tags` output, Git accepts `%` in a tag, and `debian/rules:55-56` invokes that build without replacing embedded `VERSION` with normalized `DEB_VERSION`. BinaryVersion and pre-cut verification use the literal filesystem path and therefore pass; the failure appears only after STOP when systemd interprets the drop-in. Standalone normally rolls back, but the release aborts; HA intentionally leaves the drained node stopped for operator rollback.

**Exact issue boundary:** exact round-trip of an accepted runtime-version token through both filesystem and systemd unit syntax. Use a strict shared release-version grammar matching actual producers and independently escape systemd `%` (and any other retained unit syntax) at the sink.

**Required tests:** accepted/rejected producer grammar; `%` and other systemd-sensitive graphical cases; generated-drop-in golden tests; `systemd-analyze verify` against a temporary unit proving the resolved executable path is byte-for-byte the intended version directory; standalone rollback and HA operator-recovery assertions.

## 10. Dangling rollback target

**Decision:** REVISE to COHORT. **Severity:** Medium if the precondition exists; materiality is conditional. **Novelty:** a new defensive boundary distinct from empty-target `#1964` and staged-generation GC `#4876`, but not individually fileable on the current trace.

**Adjudication:** the mechanism is real. `readCurrentVersion` returns `filepath.Base` of the symlink target without proving it is a bare target or that `versions/<target>` is complete (`pkg/upgrade/runner.go:290-301`). Fresh-cut guards check only nonempty/safe text (`pkg/upgrade/cutover.go:374-407,511-537`), and rollback flips to `PreviousVersion` without a previous-directory preflight (`pkg/upgrade/flip.go:125-161`). A dangling/incomplete target plus a failed new start can therefore leave xpfd offline.

The MATERIAL trace does not clear the supported-producer gate. Normal seed and copy publish complete directories by atomic rename; flip atomically repoints `current`; normal versions GC protects current/target/previous; packaging teardown removes the link as part of explicit downgrade/purge rather than leaving a live supported layout dangling. The source trace requires storage corruption, an interrupted manual repair, or malformed persisted state. The upgrade module intentionally contains corruption defenses, so this is worthwhile fail-closed hardening, but it is not a fresh individually fileable availability defect without a supported writer or routine fault that creates the state.

**Exact cohort boundary:** validate a rollback target as a bare in-tree symlink target with the complete lockstep runtime before any fresh or resumed live mutation, and revalidate before DB restoration/rollback. Do not merge unrelated staged-generation or empty-first-cut issues.

**Required tests:** dangling target, pathful target, non-directory, missing `xpfd`, missing helper, unreadable target, persisted resume, and failure-then-rollback. Assert refusal occurs before STOP and before destructive DB restore. A future concrete supported producer should promote this item back to MATERIAL.

## 11. Web-management interface identity

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; closed `#4047/#5127` own unauthenticated off-loopback clamping, not Junos-to-kernel identity resolution.

**Adjudication:** `resolveAPIBinds` passes authored `HTTPInterface`/`HTTPSInterface` directly to `resolveInterfaceAddr` (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1374-1397`). That helper calls `net.InterfaceByName` on the literal and silently falls back to loopback on failure (`pkg/daemon/daemon_cluster_bind.go:17-50`). Supported config preserves references such as `ge-0/0/0.0` verbatim (`pkg/config/compiler_system.go:455-475`), while the canonical resolver maps slash names, unit 0, VLAN, RETH, IRB, XFRM, and tunnel identities to Linux names (`pkg/config/types.go:132-235`). A literal Junos physical name cannot exist on Linux because `/` is forbidden. Strict auth validation permits the authenticated bind, startup succeeds, and the requested remote REST service instead listens only on loopback.

**Exact issue boundary:** every web-management interface reference must resolve through the canonical committed-config-to-kernel identity owner before address lookup. Invalid/missing references must produce an explicit degraded/readiness state or strict commit failure; the unauthenticated loopback safety clamp remains intact.

**Required tests:** pure resolved bind-address tests for physical unit 0, VLAN, RETH local member, IRB bridge, tunnel/XFRM, IPv4, and scoped IPv6. Include a missing-interface tolerant-load case that remains loopback but reports degradation, and a strict-config undefined-reference rejection if adopted.

## 12. Web-management listener/service port contract

**Decision:** APPROVE. **Severity:** Medium. **Gate:** MATERIAL. **Novelty:** new; `#5566` is established-session retention, `#5644` is absent/stale nft publication, and neither owns wrong service tuples.

**Adjudication:** web management binds HTTP/HTTPS to 8080/8443 (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1378-1397`), and `pkg/api/server.go:528-558,577-620` opens those exact listeners. The host-inbound SSOT maps `http`/`webapi-clear-text` to TCP/80 and `https`/`webapi-ssl` to TCP/443 (`pkg/config/host_inbound_tokens.go:325-350`). Nft rendering emits those accepts followed by a destination-address catch-all drop (`pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go:917-967,1044-1087`), and the Rust local-delivery classifier independently admits only 80/443 (`userspace-dp/src/afxdp/forwarding/host_inbound.rs:97-114`). No proxy, redirect, or DNAT connects the port pairs.

This root is independently reachable with a kernel-compatible configured interface, so it does not depend on issue 11. On an ordinary zoned, non-lifeline interface, least-privilege `https` admits an unused 443 socket while dropping the actual 8443 listener. `all` and lifeline bypasses are overbroad/special-case workarounds, not fulfillment of the named-service contract.

**Exact issue boundary:** one cross-package contract connecting configured web-management listeners with Go nft and Rust host-inbound service tuples. Choose standard external 80/443 for vSRX parity or define `webapi-*` semantics for 8080/8443 without changing unrelated generic HTTP/HTTPS services; do not emit ports with no corresponding enabled listener.

**Required tests:** build listener addresses and both host-inbound classifiers from the same HTTP/HTTPS config; prove the actual listener ports are admitted and adjacent ports denied without `all`. Cover HTTP-only, HTTPS-only, dual-stack, disabled service, lifeline negative control, interface override, Go/Rust parity, and no-listener/no-admit behavior.

## RHA-01: hard-local readiness bypass

**Evidence:** `pkg/cluster/manager.go:53-70` defines one composite Ready bit.
`pkg/cluster/election.go:308-320` checks it with a peer, but
`pkg/cluster/election.go:359-405`, especially 386-403, bypasses it when
`peerAlive` is false and publishes Primary. The bypass is pinned by
`pkg/cluster/election_test.go:779-817`. Local VIP/interface/userspace inputs
are at `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:20-64`,
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:269-314`, and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:610-630`.

**Trace:** localReady=false -> cold boot/asymmetric heartbeat loss -> no peer ->
`electSingleNode` skips Ready -> Primary/activation. Both isolated nodes can
take the same branch.

**Hostile refutation/scenarios:** survivor availability may waive peer-sync
freshness, not local dataplane arm, required interfaces, or VIP capability.
Cold boot, timeout, reconnect, and split-brain checks therefore fail; frames and
mixed versions cannot protect a local branch.

**Dedup/fix:** #103 has the same trigger, cause, impact, and remedy, including
an acceptance criterion forbidding peer-loss promotion while unready. Reopen it.
#5641 concerns readiness construction and #5275 one readiness producer. Split
hard-local from peer-dependent readiness; always gate on the former and test
simultaneous no-peer startup.

## RHA-02: unacknowledged heartbeat fence

**Evidence:** `pkg/cluster/heartbeat_manager.go:358-448` elects/activates at
425-426 and invokes fencing only at 428-446.
`pkg/cluster/sync_failover.go:379-397` sends a one-way `syncMsgFence`;
`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:1657-1662` has no applied ACK.
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_sync.go:877-908` only attempts dataplane RG demotion,
discards errors, and does not atomically revoke cluster/VRRP/direct-VIP
authority.

**Trace:** B times out still-forwarding A -> B becomes active -> B writes Fence
-> write may fail/delay or A may apply partially -> both retain authority.

**Hostile refutation/scenarios:** a successful write is not receipt or applied
fencing. Duplicate/out-of-order fences have no epoch; reconnect cannot reorder
already-published ownership; mixed peers negotiate no ACK. This is the direct
asymmetric split-brain and timeout/fence failure.

**Dedup/fix:** closed #72 describes the same heartbeat trigger, unfenced peer,
dual-active impact, and gate-on-ack remedy. Reopen it. #5640 is planned
failover; closed #3917 fixed the receiver's RG set only. Add a takeover epoch
and full-authority applied ACK, or proven external fence, before activation.

## RHA-03: failed item completes bulk epoch

**Evidence:** `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:321-365` consumes fallible
`PutClusterSynced` results in void helpers. At 1371-1423 a key enters
`bulkRecvV4/V6` before install. At 1458-1499 BulkEnd reconciles, ACKs, sets
`bulkEverCompleted`, and fires readiness without install debt.
`pkg/cluster/sync.go:828-873` reconciles from received keys.
`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_ha.go:936-964` exposes helper errors but a
later success can clear coarse health.

**Trace:** BulkStart(E) -> record K -> K install fails -> another item succeeds
-> BulkEnd(E) preserves K as “present” -> ACK/readiness, though K is absent.

**Hostile refutation/scenarios:** logging/coarse health cannot prove repair of
K. Partial transfer and helper timeout are direct; duplicate delivery repairs
only accidentally; reconnect may skip a new cold prime (#5480). Failover loses
selected flows.

**Dedup/fix:** #346 has the same helper failure, false success/readiness, and
propagate-or-track remedy; its logging fix was insufficient. Reopen it. #5272
is no active transaction; #5305 is partial mutation within Put; #4084 assumed
normal asynchronous success. Track epoch failure/successful keys, withhold ACK
and readiness, and authoritatively retry or restart the bounded epoch.

## RHA-04: unordered replace-all state

**Evidence:** every fabric gets a receive loop at
`pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:475-536`; `activeConnLocked` at 414-420 selects
send only. IPsec/DHCP messages replace state unconditionally at 1559-1584.
`pkg/cluster/sync.go:302-320,902-1048` stores no incarnation/sequence and
DHCP stamps delayed content with a fresh receive time at 1005-1020. Wire
payloads at `pkg/cluster/sync_protocol.go:569-598,781-829` carry no order.
Consumers are `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:349-365,1543-1555` and
`pkg/daemon/daemon_dhcp_lease_sync.go:325-400`.

**Trace:** F0 stalls with S1 -> F1 delivers S2 -> delayed F0 delivers S1 ->
receiver replaces newer state with older state -> failover seeds stale leases
or SA state.

**Hostile refutation/scenarios:** TCP orders one stream, not F0 versus F1.
Reconnect and out-of-order full frames are sufficient; duplicates are safe only
when identical. Peer reboot/mixed version has no epoch reset contract.

**Dedup/fix:** #5084 is queued config apply ordering; #5274 is session/config
epoch; #3931 was config goroutine order; #4385 was missing empty IPsec set.
Retain new. Add authenticated peer incarnation and per-type sequence through a
legacy-safe new envelope/message type.

## RHA-05: shutdown races RG reconciliation

**Evidence:** `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:641-645` launches untracked
`reconcileRGStateLoop`. Shutdown at 819-850 waits only tracked goroutines,
then clears RG/VIP ownership at 916-963. `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha.go:488-510`
checks cancellation only between passes, while 555-700 uses
`context.Background()` for actuation. Normal synchronized VIP ownership is at
`pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:112-203`.

**Trace:** pass snapshots “active” -> shutdown cancels -> cleanup deactivates
and removes VIP -> unjoined pass resumes and reactivates/readds -> peer takes
over while old ownership survives.

**Hostile refutation/scenarios:** cancellation cannot stop an in-flight
background-context call. Partial teardown, shutdown timeout, cold-start
reconcile, and split ownership remain possible.

**Dedup/fix:** #5308 names scheduler/RPM loops and different operational state;
do not inflate it into an all-goroutines umbrella. Retain new. Track/join this
loop, propagate shutdown context, then perform one serialized final ownership
cleanup under the normal VIP state owner.

## RHA-06: unreadable trial journal fails open

**Evidence:** `pkg/daemon/kernel_selfrecover.go:38-53` returns on runner or
`IsArmed` error without HA hold/recovery. Startup proceeds into first
config/election at `pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go:1582-1603`.
`pkg/upgrade/kernel_run.go:20-34,357-366,619-627` shows persistent journal,
arm, and read-error paths. `cmd/xpfd/upgrade_kernel.go:115-127` returns an
error, but `scripts/image/xpf-kernel-promote:34-58` can exit zero and
`scripts/image/xpf-kernel-promote.service:8-29` then skips OnFailure.

**Trace:** armed trial -> candidate boot -> corrupt/unreadable journal ->
recovery returns -> election/ownership on unvalidated kernel; script status can
also suppress recovery.

**Hostile refutation/scenarios:** blanket fail-closed on any absent file could
deadlock both nodes, but positive trial/boot evidence plus unknown journal is
not “not armed.” Cold boot, partial write, schema/mixed version, and failover
readiness fail.

**Dedup/fix:** #4872 covers other kernel-roll branches, not this tri-state
persistence/exit seam; retain new. Model armed/not-armed/unknown, correlate with
boot-slot evidence, hold/retry or boot known-good on a bounded policy, and
preserve failure through systemd.

## RHA-07: old stream defeats delete generation

**Evidence:** `pkg/cluster/sync_conn.go:304-320` admits guard/apply/record is
non-atomic based on a single-receiver assumption, while 475-536 retains both

`pkg/dataplane/session_store.go:50-69,499-525` deletes the current key without

F0 key-only delete resumes -> removes I2 in Go and helper.

## Findings

### Z1-F01

**Title:** Split top-level roots bypass stable-ID collision gates and silently quarantine or drop committed zones, VRFs, and tunnels

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** All three collision gates collect only the first applicable top-level root. `zoneid.go:91,124`, `routinginstanceid.go:95,124`, and `tunnelid.go:177,242` call `ConfigTree.FindChild`, whose contract at `ast.go:129-137` returns the first match. Their node-expanded views repeat the same first-root lookup. In contrast, `compiler_dispatch.go:31-57` compiles every `security`, `interfaces`, and `routing-instances` root in author order. A disposable public-parser harness proved the differential: single-root `z174`/`z214`, `wg78.0`/`wg1408.0`, and dynamically found VRF colliders were rejected; equivalent split-root inputs returned `strict_error=<nil>`. The split-zone config retained two zones, the split-tunnel config retained two emitted endpoint names, and the split-VRF config returned success after `compiler_routing.go:482-512` quarantined one instance and appended only a warning.

**Trace:** 1. Parse hierarchical input with a benign first `security`/`interfaces`/`routing-instances` root and a colliding identity in a second root. 2. Every strict stable-ID view reads only root one, so no pair exists at the gate. 3. `compileSections` lowers both roots. 4. Zone snapshot quarantine removes the later zone, unzones its interfaces, and removes/prunes its policies (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/zones_quarantine.go:28-126`); tunnel publication drops the later endpoint through `usedIDs` (`tunnels.go:39-48,113-118`); routing-instance lowering itself drops the later VRF (`compiler_routing.go:492-510`). 5. Strict commit reports success although configured isolation/forwarding objects are absent from live state.

**Refutation attempt:** The duplicate-named-block gate does not help: the reproductions use distinct names that collide only after stable hashing, and `dup_named_blocks.go` has no cross-root stable-ID union. Group views do not help because their post-expansion collectors again call `FindChild`. Schema validation permits repeated top-level blocks, and the parser deliberately appends them. The runtime belts prevent an ID alias from merging two security domains, but that refutes only a cross-domain leak, not the green strict commit followed by deterministic object loss. Both `CompileConfig` and `CompileConfigForNode` call the same deficient gates. The harness used known frozen collision pairs and a dynamically verified VRF pair, so it does not depend on a hash assumption.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is cold config work. Enumerating all matching roots, or canonicalizing same-name top-level roots before every gate and compiler, remains O(AST size) and adds no packet-path work. The violated invariant is that strict admission and typed lowering must consume the same complete root set.

**Why it matters:** A configuration accepted as valid can lose an entire zone and its policies, a routing instance and its routes, or a tunnel endpoint at publication. Runtime handling is fail-closed, but the resulting outage and config/live divergence are material production behavior.

**Fix direction:** Replace first-match top-level lookups in all three collectors and node-expanded views with iterate-all traversal, preferably through one canonical top-level-root iterator shared by strict gates and section compilation. Add single-root/split-root equivalence tests for each frozen collision and assert strict rejection before any quarantine belt runs.

**Labels:** `bug`, `config`, `zones`, `routing`, `tunnels`, `validation`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** This shares the general duplicate-root invariant class with `A3-b00-F001`, but not its state owners or repair boundary: that finding owns interface range/unsupported/unit prepasses and interface replacement; this finding owns three stable-hash identity gates and zone/VRF/tunnel quarantine. #3075, #3855, #1873, and #1914 established the gates but do not own their multi-root bypass. No exact match appeared in the supplied indexes or refreshed 208-open-issue search. A coordinator may choose one umbrella issue for all first-root gates, but the production state and required regression set must include this distinct slice.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. At fresh tip `fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`, every cited config and userspace file is unchanged from the reviewed base; the only tip change is unrelated policy-simulator predefined-set expansion.

### A3-b00-F001

**Title:** First-root-only interface prepasses bypass QinQ rejection, erase range-applied filters, and leave the #5631 alias repair bypassable

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `compiler_interface_range.go:55-61`, `compiler_interfaces_unsupported.go:86-93`, and the new `compiler_interface_unit_alias.go:75-82` all stop at the first `interfaces` root. `compiler_dispatch.go:31-41` compiles every root, while `compiler_interfaces.go` replaces a same-named typed interface on a later pass. The prior QinQ and range/filter harness traces remain valid; source inspection additionally shows that M23/#5631's repair can be bypassed by placing one numeric unit spelling in a later top-level root.

**Trace:** A benign first root hides a second-root `inner-vlan-id`, so strict commit succeeds although the one-tag shim path cannot enforce the intended inner policy. Separately, first-root interface-range expansion installs a shared input filter, then a later root recompiles the member and replaces the typed interface with no filter. For #5631, distinct aliases split across roots evade the raw-AST collision gate and converge on the same int-keyed unit during lowering.

**Refutation attempt:** `validateDuplicateNamedBlockAST` cannot reject the QinQ case because interface names differ, and it runs before a range creates its member. The range trace has no authored duplicate member block at gate time. Schema validation accepts the typed inner-VLAN leaf before the intended unsupported gate, and no tail validator rechecks it. Snapshot builders copy the final typed filter field verbatim. The #5631 tests cover aliases inside one root only; their passing result does not exercise split roots.

**HPC/invariant check:** Canonicalize or gather all interface roots once, then expand/validate/compile the union in linear time. Repeated root-by-root rescans or Cartesian range replay are unnecessary. No packet-path work is required.

**Why it matters:** Strict admission can permit unsupported QinQ traffic to avoid userspace policy and can remove an input filter from a live addressed interface. The latter is a direct firewall fail-open. The incomplete unit-alias repair retains order-dependent filter ownership.

**Fix direction:** Normalize every top-level `interfaces` node into one merge-preserving view before range expansion, unsupported checks, alias checks, and typed lowering. Add split-root QinQ, range/member, and unit-alias regressions that assert the emitted userspace snapshot.

**Labels:** `bug`, `config`, `interfaces`, `firewall`, `userspace-dp`, `security`, `vsrx-parity`

### A3-b01-C1

**Title:** Address and address-set names share an untagged reference namespace but compile into address-first shadowing

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `compiler_security_addressbook.go:286-337` stores addresses and sets in separate maps without a cross-kind uniqueness check. Policy validation accepts either kind and resolves an address before a set; the live resolver in `pkg/dataplane/userspace/capabilities.go:217-236` uses the same address-first order. A reference retains only the string, so its authored kind cannot be recovered later.

**Trace:** Define `address X` for one prefix and `address-set X` containing additional members. Reference `X` from a deny. Strict/schema admission succeeds, typed policy keeps `"X"`, strict expansion and live snapshot expansion select the single address, and the rest of the intended set falls through to a later permit/default permit.

**Refutation attempt:** Same-kind duplicate and recursive-set gates do not establish cross-kind uniqueness. Feed overlay handling does not disambiguate the static name. Both strict and live consumers were checked, so consistent address-first behavior is not a safety defense: it is the deterministic narrowing. A tagged reference does not exist in `PolicyMatch` or NAT match DTOs.

**HPC/invariant check:** A cross-kind map-key check is O(number of address entries) at commit and has no packet cost. The violated invariant is injective, canonical object identity.

**Why it matters:** A deny intended for an address set can cover only one same-named address, allowing other members through.

**Fix direction:** Strictly reject address/address-set cross-kind collisions. On tolerant load, warn and quarantine the ambiguous name rather than selecting a kind. Longer term, preserve a tagged reference through policy and NAT lowering.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `config`, `address-book`, `dataplane`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** Missing-reference, recursive-set, feed-overlay #4925, and same-kind duplicate owners have different causes and fixes. No exact cross-kind shadow owner appeared in the supplied or refreshed issue sets.

### A3-b02-F01

**Title:** Direct-host deny resolves a user application as the same-named predefined application-set

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `junos_host_deny.go:690-733` calls `ResolveApplicationSet` before `junosHostReduceApp` calls `ResolveApplication`. Strict policy validation (`compiler_validate_strict_policy.go:183-201`) and live userspace lowering (`capabilities.go:403-423`) do the opposite: application first, set second. `predefined.go` intentionally allows a user application to shadow a predefined set name.

**Fix direction:** Use a shared application-first resolver that returns the selected object kind and expanded members. Add compiler-to-direct-host projection and nft rendering regressions for the shadow case.
