### A3-b03-F001

**Title:** Qualified-next-hop preference is dropped at the live AF_XDP snapshot boundary, so a floating backup becomes ECMP

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `types_routing.go:202-220` and `compiler_routing.go:307-350` preserve per-candidate preference. `pkg/dataplane/userspace/routes.go:75-90` serializes only address/interface strings plus route-level preference, and `protocol.go:1292-1310` has no candidate-level field. Rust `protocol/snapshot.rs:153-171` is identical; `forwarding_build/fib.rs:280-309` creates unannotated candidates, and `forwarding/mod.rs:2772-2791` hashes across all live candidates.

**Trace:** Commit a normal primary next hop and a qualified backup with preference 250. Typed compilation marks only the backup with that preference. Go emits one route with two indistinguishable next-hop strings and route preference 5. Rust builds one candidate vector; while both neighbors are live, flow hashes select both instead of using only the primary.

**Refutation attempt:** FRR renders the distance correctly, but AF_XDP is the live transit authority and does not consult FRR's selection. Route-level sorting cannot recover metadata discarded inside one route. Liveness cannot restore priority while both paths are reachable. No strict gate rejects this valid grammar, and the wire has no hidden field from which to reconstruct it.

**HPC/invariant check:** Carry a compact per-candidate preference and scan the already bounded candidate slice for the lowest live tier, then hash only inside that tier. This remains allocation-free with bounded per-packet work.

**Why it matters:** Production traffic can use an expensive, constrained, or policy-distinct backup while the primary is healthy.

**Fix direction:** Extend the Go/Rust route wire and FIB candidate types with preference presence/value. Add both-live, primary-down, and same-tier ECMP tests across compiler, snapshot, and Rust selection.

**Labels:** `bug`, `routing`, `dataplane`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** #3871 repaired compiler and FRR rendering; this is the later live AF_XDP publication/selection boundary. No exact open owner exists.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. Every cited Go and Rust blob is unchanged at fresh tip.

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `schema_chassis.go:181-199` gives the `redundancy-group <id>` and nested `node <id>` identity slots no key validator, although `schema_walk.go` supports typed keys. `compiler_system.go:1874-1909` initializes each failed `Atoi` to zero. `compiler_validate_strict_chassis.go:65-135` then sees valid effective ID 0 and valid priority, with parse provenance already erased.

**Trace:** Commit `redundancy-group bogus node typo priority 200`. Schema accepts both identities, lowering emits group 0 and node-priority key 0, strict semantic bounds pass, and the cluster runtime consumes RG0/node0 state. A real RG0 definition can converge on the same live map key with order-dependent election inputs.

**Refutation attempt:** Top-level `chassis cluster node` typing is a different leaf. The #4434 gate catches numeric out-of-range IDs but cannot distinguish malformed text that became zero. Cardinality does not enforce effective-ID uniqueness, and lenient compatibility is irrelevant because strict admission accepts the input.

**HPC/invariant check:** Typed key checks and effective-ID uniqueness are bounded by the existing 255-group limit and add no heartbeat or packet-path cost.

**Why it matters:** A typo can reconfigure RG0/node0 election state and cause unexpected failover or RETH/VIP outage.

**Fix direction:** Attach integer key validators for group 0..255 and node 0..1, retain a semantic uniqueness/provenance backstop, and test flat/hierarchical nonnumeric, signed, noncanonical, out-of-range, and duplicate-effective forms.

**Labels:** `bug`, `ha`, `config-compiler`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** #4434 owns numeric wire bounds; #5631 owns interface-unit aliases. Neither owns chassis nonnumeric-to-zero identity coercion.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. Schema, compiler, strict gate, and cluster consumer are unchanged at fresh tip.

### A3-b02-F03

**Title:** Strict GARP count accepts an effectively unbounded raw-socket work budget per VIP

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `schema_chassis.go:200-216` deliberately applies only `ValidateIntegerMin(1)` despite documenting Junos 1..16. `compiler_system.go:1910-1915` retains any architecture-sized accepted value. `pkg/cluster/garp.go:159-216,233-255,482-560` opens a raw socket and runs `count-1` 50ms follow-ups; `pkg/vrrp/instance.go:2280-2304` and `pkg/daemon/daemon_ha_vip.go:546-565` pass the configured count per VIP.

**Trace:** Strictly commit an enormous positive count with multiple RETH VIPs. On ownership transition, each VIP opens a socket and launches a long-lived goroutine. While ownership remains valid, the abdication predicate stays true and each loop keeps sending at 50ms cadence, retaining its fd until the configured iteration count drains.

**Refutation attempt:** The #2867/#2898 predicate stops work after abdication or supersession, not during normal ownership. OS fd limits merely turn later opens into failures after existing loops have consumed resources. #5087 may ignore a day-2 count change, but fresh boot, instance recreation, and direct mode still consume it. The text-size limit does not bound an integer's semantic work.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is asynchronous control-plane/network work, not AF_XDP packet work, but it is unbounded in iteration time and per-VIP fd/goroutine fanout. A runtime clamp and matching strict validator are O(1).

**Why it matters:** One accepted value can cause sustained L2 traffic and long-lived fd/goroutine consumption during HA convergence.

**Fix direction:** Clamp before fanout, make strict validation match the runtime bound (Junos 1..16 is the natural default), warn-and-clamp on tolerant load, and bound aggregate outstanding bursts per interface/RG.

**Labels:** `bug`, `ha`, `resource-exhaustion`, `config-compiler`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** #5087 owns day-2 reconciliation; #2867 owns abdication cancellation; #5090 owns VRRP address-count wire wrap. No exact GARP work-budget owner exists.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. Admission and all direct runtime consumers are unchanged at fresh tip.

## Publication architecture trace

1. `commitAndApply`, `commitConfirmedAndApply`, and peer `syncAndApply` promote
   and persist the accepted config before `applyConfigLocked` runs. The active
   store is therefore desired truth even if host/dataplane actuation later
   fails (`daemon_apply.go:302-354, 2095-2114`).
2. The daemon serializes apply with `applySem`. It reconciles VRFs and interface
   topology, prepares route and feed overlays, then calls the runtime
   dataplane. Feed producers are reconciled before `SnapshotForBindings` is
   read (`daemon_apply.go:735-788, 865-887`; `daemon_feeds.go:74-136`).
3. `Manager.Compile` builds one `ConfigSnapshot` containing interfaces, zones,
   policies/address books, NAT, feeds, routes, neighbors, screens, filters,
   mirrors, tunnels, CoS, flow, HA capability state, and wire protocol data
   (`builder.go:29-158`). It programs shim/classifier state, starts or reuses the
   helper, sends `apply_snapshot`, and advances `lastSnapshot`, published/applied
   generation, indexes, and hash only after a positive response
   (`manager_compile.go:162-377`).
4. Every main control request uses a fresh Unix connection. A write may reach
   the helper and mutate live state before Go loses or times out reading the
   response, so a Go error is an *unknown acknowledgement*, not proof of no
   application (`process_control.go:80-143`). The session channel has the same
   request/response shape under a separate mutex (`:146-185`).
5. After the full dataplane call, the daemon reconciles Linux policy-routing
   rules and then performs a second routes-only publication. That publisher
   clones `lastSnapshot`, replaces only routes and config metadata, and marks
   the result applied after ACK (`daemon_apply.go:759-771, 1455-1508`;
   `manager_overlay.go:95-196`). This is the #5642 repair and the source of the
   F02/F03 failure boundaries.
6. Route-cache invalidation is a second acknowledged operation. The reusable
   API explicitly requires caller-owned retry debt on failure
   (`manager_generation.go:40-119`). The ip-monitoring caller implements that
   contract; the new #5642 caller does not (`daemon_ipmon.go:264-352`).
7. lo0 and host-inbound policy are rendered after the dataplane/routing phases
   as **two separate** `nft -f -` transactions. Each table replacement is atomic
   and preserves its previous table on failure, but the two tables and the Rust
   snapshot do not share one kernel transaction (`daemon_nft.go:21-52,
   89-154, 216-318`; `daemon_apply.go:1854-1867,2085-2092`). Day-2 errors are
   returned; cold-boot absence remains exact #5644.
8. The status loop can retry only a candidate already owned by
   `m.lastSnapshot` with `publishedSnapshot < lastSnapshot.Generation`, plus
   explicitly modeled worker-arm debt. It cannot reconstruct an ordinary full
   candidate discarded before ACK, a route-only candidate never stored, or a
   forgotten FIB bump (`process_status.go:11-178`).
9. HA takeover readiness checks helper process/capabilities/armed state, mode,
   XSK liveness/bindings, and session-mirror health, but does not compare the
   store's active config identity to the helper's acknowledged applied config
   (`manager_ha.go:269-330`; `daemon_ha_userspace_readiness.go:215-232`).

This trace refutes a single-generation invariant today: accepted config,
helper snapshot, Linux route rules, nft tables, flow-cache generation, and HA
readiness can represent different generations without one durable debt owner.

## Required adjudications

### D-A6-F1 versus #5645

**Verdict: DUP, specifically an incomplete acceptance matrix for M38/#5645.
Reopen #5645; do not file a new issue.**

The technical observation is corroborated. `SnapshotForBindings` skips each
missing/unready feed, publishes when the flattened union is merely nonempty,
and never checks every configured `FeedNames` member's `hasSnapshot`
(`feeds.go:457-501`). One ready member therefore masks a never-ready member.
If the binding name also exists in the static address book, omission of every
unready feed still leaves that name representable and publishes the static
subset (`policies_addrbook.go:161-224`; `policies_representable.go:119-157`). A
deny can under-match in both cases.

The strict four-part duplicate gate nevertheless matches #5645:

| Duplicate dimension | M38/#5645 | D-A6-F1 residual | Adjudication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Root cause | First-success readiness is lost when publishing a feed-bound name. | Readiness is collapsed to any nonempty constituent/static content. | Same completeness/readiness root. |
| State owner | `feeds.Manager` / `SnapshotForBindings`. | Same manager and accessor. | Same owner. |
| Impact class | Feed-backed deny becomes match-none/under-matches and fails open. | Feed-backed deny enforces only a ready/static subset and fails open. | Same authorization impact. |
| Remediation boundary | Do not publish the binding until authoritative feed content is ready; retain unresolved/tainted state. | Require every configured constituent ready and preserve taint through static merge. | Same readiness barrier, broadened tests. |

The closed issue body explicitly owns a direct feed-backed deny before first
success. The merged repair implemented only the all-unready feed-only case.
Multi-feed ready+unready and static+unready are fail-on-fix acceptance cases,
not a new root, owner, impact, or conceptual fix boundary. #5646 remains
separate because it owns desired/applied callback acknowledgement after a
snapshot has been fetched.

### D-A6-F2/F3 and D-A7-F01

**Verdict: two root/fix boundaries, not one and not three.**

| Boundary | Included observations | Independent invariant and fix |
|---|---|---|
| A: full/partial snapshot provenance | D-A6-F2 and the hybrid half of D-A7-F01 | A routes-only snapshot may derive only from a positively acknowledged full snapshot of the same config. Guard the partial call on full-apply success/identity, or order rules before one full publication. |
| B: staged route reconciliation debt | D-A6-F3 and the publish/bump half of D-A7-F01 | Kernel-rule change, helper route publish, and FIB invalidation remain owed until all are acknowledged. Return/join errors and persist one staged route/FIB debt owner. |

D-A7-F01 is a useful cross-layer umbrella but spans both boundaries. It is not
a third fileable issue. Collapsing A and B is also wrong: a same-generation
provenance guard can leave route publish/bump failures forgotten, while a
perfect retry latch can repeatedly publish a hybrid baseline unless provenance
is fixed. D-A6-F3's publish-failure and bump-failure legs *do* belong together:
they are consecutive stages of one route-reconciliation transaction and share
one state owner and completion predicate.

One correction to D-A6-F2's prose is material: the ordinary initial
`ApplyConfig` error is **not eventually returned**. The local `err` at
`daemon_apply.go:903-909` is recorded and then dropped; the tail can return nil.
That correction supports fresh F01 below and strengthens F02's successful-
commit impact.

## Findings

### Z2-F01

**Title:** Ordinary full userspace snapshot failure can report a successful commit and leave old policy HA-ready

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** The active config is already promoted/persisted when apply begins
(`daemon_apply.go:302-305,2110-2114`). At `daemon_apply.go:900-912`, an ordinary
`d.dp.ApplyConfig` error is assigned to a block-local variable, sent only to
`recordCompileFailure`, and returned only if it is a required protocol-gate
sentinel. No dataplane error is threaded into `applyTailReconciles`, whose final
join contains only networkd, DHCP, nft, IPsec, and interface errors
(`:2085-2092`). The existing test deliberately asserts that an unrelated
compile failure is outside `compileErrorMustAbortApply`
(`compile_error_policy_test.go:11-33`).

On a pre-ACK failure, `Manager.Compile` returns before installing the candidate
as `lastSnapshot` (`manager_compile.go:199-201,323-327`), so the status loop has
no desired full candidate to retry (`process_status.go:11-39,162-178`).
`recordCompileFailure` is observability only. After any earlier success,
`/health` remains HTTP 200 because degradation is gated on
`!EverSucceeded && FailureCount>0` (`daemon_health.go:79-125`;
`api/health.go:10-39`). HA takeover checks no active-config/applied-config
identity (`manager_ha.go:279-313`).

**Trace:** C0 permits a flow and is acknowledged by the helper. An operator or
peer commits valid C1 that tightens it to deny. The store promotes C1. The full
helper request receives a pre-apply NACK, dial failure, decode failure, or
oversize rejection, so the manager retains only C0. The daemon records a
warning, continues every later reconcile, clears sessions against C1, may push
C1 to the peer, and returns success if the tail is otherwise clean. New flows
still consult C0's permit. No status tick can rebuild C1 because the rejected
candidate was never retained. On a standby, the helper can remain armed with
ready bindings and pass takeover readiness while the store advertises C1 and
the helper enforces C0. Recovery requires an unrelated apply/restart.

**Refutation attempt:** Previous-good is not fail closed relative to a
tightening. Session invalidation removes old flows but cannot make new flows
consult C1. Required protocol errors are handled, but ordinary snapshot-build,
map, process, socket, helper-NACK, and status-application errors are explicitly
outside that sentinel set. Compile health neither owns retry state nor returns
503 after a prior success. The status loop can only replay `lastSnapshot`, and
takeover readiness checks liveness rather than config identity. #4036 reduced
one false-timeout trigger but did not create desired-generation debt. The High
authorization/HA trace therefore survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** Apply/retry is config-cold. Persisting a desired config
identity and one full-snapshot retry candidate adds no packet-path allocation,
lock, scan, or atomic. The invariant is acknowledgement before success: active
config Cn must have either an acknowledged helper Cn or explicit fail-closed
debt that blocks readiness and keeps retrying.

**Why it matters:** A successful security-policy commit and subsequent HA
takeover can enforce an older permit set indefinitely. Operator, peer, health,
and forwarding truth disagree at the primary authorization boundary.

**Fix direction:** Continue independent tail reconciles, but retain the
ordinary dataplane error as a deferred `dataplaneErr` and join it into the
commit result. Persist desired full-snapshot identity/debt and have the status
owner rebuild and republish the active config until helper ACK, including
post-apply ACK-loss reconciliation. Gate HA readiness and peer applied/high-
water claims on that acknowledged identity. Add fail-once pre-apply NACK,
post-apply ACK loss, local commit, peer-sync, health, and takeover tests.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `daemon`, `ha`, `transactional-apply`, `retry`

**Dedup note:** Fresh searches found no exact owner. #4959 and #5485 own
classifier-map/XDP side effects before rejection; #5646 owns feed callback
revision ACK; #5648 owns stale re-arm capability; #5275 owns boot `Start`/arm
failure. None owns the dropped ordinary full-apply error, absent desired
candidate, successful commit, and HA config-identity gap.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. All cited lane blobs are identical at
`fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`; the direct API health predicate is
unchanged at that tip.

### Z2-F02

**Title:** The #5642 partial publisher can mark an old-policy/new-route hybrid as the new applied config

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** After the swallowed full apply error above, the daemon
unconditionally reconciles route rules and calls `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot`
(`daemon_apply.go:754-771`). `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` shallow-clones
`m.lastSnapshot`, stamps the incoming config and new generation, and rebuilds
only `Routes` (`manager_overlay.go:146-159`). Policies, NAT, address books,
interfaces, feeds, zones, filters, and capabilities remain from the prior
snapshot. After the second request ACK it sets `lastSnapshot`,
`publishedSnapshot`, `publishedPlanKey`, and applied NAT/config bookkeeping to
that hybrid (`:169-190`).

**Trace:** C0 contains a permit and a rib-group leak. C1 removes the leak and
tightens the permit to deny. The full C1 request fails before ACK, leaving C0 as
the manager baseline; this may be a true pre-apply failure or an ambiguous lost
response after C1 landed. Kernel rule reconciliation succeeds. The second
request clones C0, substitutes C1 metadata and leak-free routes, and is
accepted. If the helper had C0, it now gets old C0 policy plus new routes; if it
had already applied C1, the second request *replays* C0 policy/NAT over C1. The
manager records the hybrid as applied, making `publishedSnapshot ==
lastSnapshot.Generation`; status retry is suppressed and the commit can return
success.

**Refutation attempt:** The partial API's hash and post-ACK bookkeeping are
sound only when its baseline is the acknowledged same config. A changed
rib-group route prevents duplicate skip. The embedded `Config=C1` is metadata,
not proof that every cloned section was built from C1. A later status report
cannot infer provenance because the hybrid generation was positively ACKed.
Returning the initial error at the end would improve truth but would not undo a
hybrid already published; therefore F01 and F02 need independent repairs. The
High policy replay survives hostile refutation.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is serialized config-cold work. A config identity
or acknowledged-base generation comparison is O(1). Reordering rule
reconciliation before one full snapshot avoids the extra control round trip
and is cheaper than preserving the two-transaction design.

**Why it matters:** A policy tightening can finish with an applied-generation
record that says C1 while live AF_XDP policy/NAT content is C0. New traffic can
use a revoked permit, and normal retry logic considers the state converged.

**Fix direction:** Prefer reconciling load-bearing next-table/rib-group rules
before building one complete snapshot. If partial publication remains, require
an explicit positively acknowledged full-snapshot config identity/generation,
reject any mismatch/unknown ACK, and never stamp a different config onto cloned
sections. Add true NACK and applied-but-ACK-lost tests that assert no second
partial publish and no applied-generation advance.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `routing`, `transactional-apply`, `generation`

**Dedup note:** Closed #5642 owns the deterministic no-fault final-rib-group
cleanup. #4959/#5485 own pre-publish BPF/link mutation; #5562 owns Rust internal
ArcSwap ordering. None owns this successful Go partial publish from an
unacknowledged prior-generation baseline.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at
`fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`; all cited lane blobs are unchanged.

### Z2-F03

**Title:** The #5642 route reconcile forgets failed helper publication or FIB invalidation

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` is void. It logs and returns on
`PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` failure, and it only logs a subsequent
`BumpFIBGeneration` error (`daemon_apply.go:1478-1508`). Neither reaches the
tail error join. The bump API explicitly says callers with retry semantics must
retry an unconfirmed shim/helper invalidation (`manager_generation.go:40-55`).
The status loop cannot retry a failed route publish because no new
`lastSnapshot` was installed, and cannot retry a bump after an already-published
snapshot (`process_status.go:11-39,162-178`). By contrast, the ip-monitoring
caller returns false and retains `pendingFIBBump` (`daemon_ipmon.go:314-346`).

**Trace:** C0 has the final inter-VRF leak. C1 removes it. The initial full
snapshot is necessarily built before the kernel rule deletion and therefore
still carries the old leak. Kernel cleanup succeeds. If route republish fails,
the helper retains the leak for new flows, the daemon forgets the desired route
generation, and the commit can succeed. If route publish succeeds but the bump
fails, new lookups see corrected routes while established flow/session caches
can retain the deleted next-table decision. No ip-monitoring event is required,
so its separate dirty owner need never run; only an unrelated future apply or
bump can heal either leg.

**Refutation attempt:** The manager leaves its overlay cache retryable after a
failed publish, but retryable data is not retry debt and this caller never
returns. The one-second status loop owns only manager generations that were
stored. Logging does not alter commit truth or convergence. Duplicate-publish
skip also cannot settle a previously failed bump without an explicit pending
bit. The two failure legs share one staged route transaction, so they are one
issue, but provenance F02 remains independent.

**HPC/invariant check:** One pending config/route hash plus stage enum is bounded
and cold. Retry can reuse the existing status cadence under `applySem`; no
packet-path work is added. Completion means kernel rule, helper route snapshot,
and FIB cache generation are all acknowledged.

**Why it matters:** Removing a route leak can report success while new or
established userspace flows continue using the deleted cross-VRF instruction.

**Fix direction:** Return and join the immediate error, and persist a staged
route-reconcile debt keyed by config identity and desired route hash. Retry
publication and then invalidation until both ACK; do not clear debt on an
unrelated callback or duplicate publish. Reuse the proven ip-monitoring dirty/
pending-bump design. Add fail-once tests for both stages.

**Labels:** `bug`, `dataplane`, `routing`, `transactional-apply`, `retry`, `vrf`

**Dedup note:** Closed #3757 owns the ip-monitoring caller's dirty loop; this is
a new direct #5642 caller outside that owner. Closed #3731/#5118 own kernel rule
write/delete errors, not helper route/FIB acknowledgement after a successful
kernel change. Fresh search found no exact open owner.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes, at
`fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`.

### Z2-F04

**Title:** Failed stale-binding clears are forgotten, preventing watchdog repair

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** During bootstrap and status application, stale
`userspace_bindings` rows are zeroed with ignored `Map.Update` results, after
which `lastBindingIndices` is replaced by only the new inventory
(`maps_sync.go:178-185,760-768`). `verifyBindingsMapLocked` walks expected
helper bindings and repairs missing expected rows; it does not enumerate extra
READY rows (`:1199-1318`). The same status application may then enable
`userspace_ctrl` (`:784-789`).

**Trace:** A plan change removes an old `(ifindex,queue)` row. A transient BPF
update failure leaves its READY slot live. The error is discarded and the
index is removed from Go's retry inventory. Control is re-enabled. Packets at
that index redirect to a slot the helper no longer owns and are lost; heartbeat
expiry changes the drop reason but does not clear the authority. Later polls
see only current helper rows, so neither cleanup nor the watchdog revisits it.

**Refutation attempt:** Helper teardown cannot mutate the Go-owned binding map.
The watchdog is intentionally one-directional and map-array iteration is not
performed. New-row failures do fail closed, which isolates the defect to stale
retirement rather than refuting it. #5486 covers ctrl-disable failure, not
forgotten stale-row ownership.

**HPC/invariant check:** Status work is cold and bounded by
`BindingArrayMaxEntries`. Retaining failed indices and retrying them is O(number
of tracked rows), with no packet-path change.

**Why it matters:** One transient map update during routine rebinding can cause
a persistent forwarding outage while status reports the new helper plan.

**Fix direction:** Make stale zeroing mandatory: on failure retain the index,
fail-close ctrl, return the error, and retry next poll. Apply the same contract
at bootstrap and add a fail-once map-update seam/test.

**Labels:** `bug`, `dataplane`, `xdp`, `bpf`, `retry`

**Dedup note:** Fresh search found no exact owner. #4894 owns queue-index alias
math; #5486 owns mandatory ctrl disable before teardown.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; `maps_sync.go` is unchanged at the
fresh tip.

### Z2-F05

**Title:** Per-request session locking lets a companion upsert interleave after an authoritative delete

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `syncSessionRequestsLocked` claims a prebuilt forward/reverse pair
is transmitted contiguously but loops over `requestSessionSync`
(`manager_ha.go:1397-1422`). That function acquires and releases `sessionMu` for
each individual fresh connection (`process_control.go:155-185`). The Rust
contract synthesizes reverse state from a forward upsert, while deleting the
forward removes both directions; an explicit reverse upsert does not recreate
the forward.

**Trace:** Go sends the forward upsert; Rust installs forward and synthesized
reverse. The per-request mutex is released. A concurrent policy clear, GC, or
operator delete acquires the socket and removes both directions, then returns.
The original goroutine reacquires the mutex and sends its already-built
explicit reverse. With no transaction/tombstone, Rust accepts it and leaves a
reverse-only stale permit after the authoritative clear completed. IPv4 and
IPv6 share the schedule.

**Refutation attempt:** A single-threaded Rust listener preserves, rather than
prevents, the harmful `forward,delete,reverse` order. Delete generation zero is
unconditional. Existing #5007 coverage proves the DTO pair is built from one
snapshot but has no competing request and no adjacency assertion. #5274's
config epoch and #5380's fresh-dial latency do not linearize a logical pair.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is control-plane socket I/O. Holding the existing
mutex once around two requests adds no round trips or packet synchronization.
Large delete chunks should remain bounded or use a helper bulk verb.

**Why it matters:** A successful policy/session clear can leave one direction
of previously authorized state installed in the live helper.

**Fix direction:** Split out a round trip that assumes `sessionMu` is held and
hold it once per logical pair, or add one atomic pair/bulk helper verb. Add a
gated-listener test forcing the competing delete for v4 and v6.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `sessions`, `ha`, `concurrency`

**Dedup note:** No exact open owner. #5274, #5380, and prior discarded-delete-
error roots have different causes and remediation boundaries.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; both lane files are byte-identical at
the fresh tip.

### Z2-F06

**Title:** A zoned/unzoned duplicate local address inherits the zoned host-inbound allow set

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `BuildUnzonedHostInboundAddrs` first collects every address in a
zoned view and then omits that address from the unzoned deny, regardless of its
second owner (`zones_host_inbound.go:353-393`). The strict duplicate-local-
address validator records only zoned owners and skips an owner with no resolved
zone (`config/dup_host_local_address.go:121-152,312-337`). nft emits zoned rules
first, then the unzoned destination-only drop; neither has an ingress predicate
for this coarse path (`daemon_nft.go:667-679,894-967`).

**Trace:** Two non-lifeline VLAN units own the same local address. One is in
zone `edge` with SSH allowed; the other is unzoned. Strict validation sees only
the zoned claim. The zoned builder emits `daddr A tcp dport 22 accept`.
Unzoned construction sees A in the zoned set and removes it, so no unzoned drop
exists for A. A packet arriving on the unzoned unit for A:22 reaches input and
matches the destination-only zoned accept, bypassing Junos' unzoned deny.

**Refutation attempt:** Linux permits the same local address on multiple
interfaces, and unzoned configured interfaces remain managed/reachable. The
example uses distinct VLAN units, avoiding the unit-0 alias in F07. Existing
ambiguity reporting compares zone views and never sees the unzoned owner.
Rule reordering cannot preserve a zoned allow while denying the same daddr on
the unzoned owner without ingress identity. The High management-plane bypass
survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is cold config/nft construction. A strict
ownership gate and deterministic lenient quarantine add no userspace packet
work. The invariant is that every addressed non-lifeline unzoned interface
denies host-bound traffic.

**Why it matters:** A service intentionally exposed only on a zoned interface
becomes reachable through an unzoned interface, bypassing host-inbound policy.

**Fix direction:** Reject zoned/unzoned duplicate ownership in strict compile.
For tolerant loads and learned addresses, quarantine the ambiguous address
from positive views or emit ingress-aware rules. Cover IPv4/IPv6, static/
learned addresses, generated ordering, and packet verdicts.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `host-inbound`, `nftables`, `zones`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** Closed #3718 owns differing sets across two zoned owners and
intentionally skips unzoned owners. Closed #4420 introduced the unzoned drop.
Open #5659 is Rust empty-zone defense in depth. None owns this kernel ownership
overlap.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; lane and direct validator blobs are
unchanged at the fresh tip.

### Z2-F07

**Title:** Live unit-0 addresses are emitted under both zone-default and interface-override policy

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** A unit zone reference also maps its base name to the zone
(`zones.go:43-83`). `buildInterfaceSnapshots` independently snapshots the base
and unit, while ordinary unit 0 resolves both to the same Linux netdev
(`interfaces.go:164-324,399-428`). Host-inbound grouping looks up overrides by
exact snapshot name and groups by effective token signature
(`zones_host_inbound.go:188-209,279-308`). Only the unit receives its exact
override. Sorted default groups are emitted before later additive override
groups, each ending in a destination-only drop (`daemon_nft.go:667-670,
917-967`).

**Trace:** `ge-0-0-0.0` owns address A in a zone with empty default and a unit
override allowing SSH. Once A is live, both base and unit snapshots read A.
The base contributes A to the empty/default group; the unit contributes A to
the SSH group. The default signature sorts first and emits `daddr A drop`
before the unit's SSH accept. New SSH is denied. With a nonempty default, any
service added only by the override is denied the same way.

**Refutation attempt:** Before the address is live, only configured unit data
may appear, but that does not refute the steady live state. Dedup is local to a
signature group, not across groups. Strict duplicate validation sees one
authored unit, not the synthetic base snapshot. Observability does not change
rule order.

**HPC/invariant check:** Normalizing one netdev to one authoritative
host-inbound identity is cold and reduces duplicate nft payload. No hot-path
cost is required.

**Why it matters:** A valid per-interface service override becomes
deterministically ineffective after address realization, creating state-
dependent management/service outage.

**Fix direction:** Give base/unit-0 one authoritative host-inbound identity or
exclude the synthetic base from grouping when the unit owns the same netdev.
Add live-address IPv4/IPv6, DHCP, empty/nonempty default, and nft-order tests.

**Labels:** `bug`, `host-inbound`, `nftables`, `interface-identity`, `vsrx-parity`

**Dedup note:** #3362 introduced grouping, #5489 owns losing-zone override
bleed, and #3718 owns distinct interface duplicate addresses. None owns one
physical/unit-0 snapshot alias.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; all cited lane blobs are unchanged.

### Z2-F08

**Title:** An unjoined RG reconcile pass can reactivate forwarding and direct VIPs during shutdown

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `daemon_run.go:641-645` starts `reconcileRGStateLoop(ctx)` without
adding it to the run wait group. Shutdown cancels and waits only that group
before clearing `rg_active`, watchdogs, and direct VIPs (`:819-850,916-963`).
The loop checks cancellation only between complete passes
(`daemon_ha.go:488-510`). An in-flight `reconcileRGState` uses
`context.Background()` for `SetRGActive`, then reconciles blackholes and direct
VIP ownership (`:555-735`). The normal direct owner is serialized by
`directVIPMu` and updates `directVIPOwned` (`daemon_ha_vip.go:162-203`), but
shutdown calls bare `directRemoveVIPs` without that mutex/state (`daemon_run.go:
946-950`).

**Trace:** A reconcile pass starts just before signal cancellation and computes
the local RG active. Shutdown cancels the context and `wg.Wait` returns because
this loop is not registered. Shutdown clears `rg_active` and removes direct
VIPs. The old pass resumes, writes `SetRGActive(...,true)` with Background,
removes blackholes, and calls `applyDirectVIPOwnership(...,true)`, re-adding
VIP/link-local/services after teardown removed them. VRRP/cluster/dataplane
then stop with host and forwarding ownership transiently or persistently
reasserted out of order.

**Refutation attempt:** Context cancellation prevents a *new* loop iteration,
not an already-entered pass. Idempotent operations do not help because the two
callers request opposite desired states. Later dataplane teardown may disable
AF_XDP, but a re-added local VIP and services remain a host ownership split and
the race can occur between clear and teardown. The direct shutdown path also
bypasses the authoritative mutex/state, so it cannot linearize against the
pass. The High HA split-brain/outage risk survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** Joining one 2-second control loop is shutdown-only.
No packet path or steady-state cadence changes. The invariant is quiescence:
all ownership writers must stop before fail-closed teardown begins.

**Why it matters:** A node being shut down can reassert traffic ownership after
the peer is expected to take over, causing split ownership, blackholing, or
service/VIP residue.

**Fix direction:** Put the RG reconcile loop in the lifecycle wait group or
give it an explicit cancel/join handle, and pass cancellation through the whole
pass. Join it before HA clear. Route shutdown direct-mode removal through the
same locked ownership state machine. Add a barrier-controlled in-flight-pass
shutdown test.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `ha`, `shutdown`, `concurrency`, `vip`, `dataplane`

**Dedup note:** Fresh search found no exact owner. #5308 joins scheduler and
pin-retry loops but does not include RG reconciliation or direct VIP ownership.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; `daemon_run.go`, `daemon_ha.go`, and
`daemon_ha_vip.go` are unchanged at the fresh tip.

### Z2-F09

**Title:** An unreadable kernel-upgrade journal disables HA candidate fencing and promotion recovery

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `holdSecondaryIfKernelCandidateArmed` returns on every `IsArmed`
error before setting the election hold (`kernel_selfrecover.go:38-50`). The
hold must precede `cluster.UpdateConfig`, which performs the first election
(`daemon_run.go:1582-1603`). Direct `upgrade/kernel_run.go:20-34,357-366,
619-627` shows permission, I/O, or JSON errors propagate from both `IsArmed`
and `Promote`. The promotion wrapper maps infrastructure exit codes to exit 0
without reboot, while its systemd `OnFailure` runs only on unit failure/timeout
(`scripts/image/xpf-kernel-promote:34-58` and `.service:8-29`).

**Trace:** A node boots an armed candidate but the journal is unreadable or
malformed. xpfd treats unknown as ordinary boot, skips the secondary hold, and
performs an election; it can claim Primary. The later promotion command gets
the same journal error. Its wrapper exits successfully without promoting,
reverting, or rebooting, suppressing systemd recovery. The unverified candidate
can continue serving indefinitely and preempt a healthy peer.

**Refutation attempt:** A genuinely missing journal maps safely to Init, but
read/parse errors are distinct and explicitly returned. Firmware `BootNext`
fallback helps only on a later reboot; the wrapper deliberately avoids one and
masks failure. Tests cover a readable armed journal, not unknown journal state
at the first election plus wrapper behavior. The High candidate-kernel fencing
failure survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is boot-cold. A tri-state journal result and
bounded retry have no forwarding-path cost. Unknown candidate state must fail
toward non-ownership.

**Why it matters:** A corrupted state file can turn a guarded kernel trial into
an indefinitely serving unverified primary, defeating the upgrade safety gate.

**Fix direction:** Preserve armed/not-armed/unknown. In HA, conservatively hold
secondary on unknown when boot evidence may indicate a trial, retry recovery
with a bound, and do not turn unresolved promotion infrastructure failure into
a green unit without a retained hold or one known-good fallback reboot. Add
daemon-election and service-wrapper tests for unreadable/malformed journals.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `ha`, `upgrade`, `kernel`, `boot`

**Dedup note:** #4872 owns destructive pruning after unreadable boot-slot
discovery; #5275 owns ordinary dataplane arm failure. Neither owns kernel-trial
journal ambiguity at election and promotion.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. The lane files and direct upgrade/
script contracts are unchanged at
`fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`.

### Z2-F10

**Title:** VRF setup failure is recorded as managed and discarded from the commit result

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** For a matching desired table, `routing.reconcileVRFs` logs
`LinkSetUp` failure as non-fatal, appends the name to the realized/managed set,
and records no error (`routing/vrf.go:228-236`, direct read). The lane caller
also logs and discards every `ReconcileVRFs` and `BindInterfaceToVRF` error,
publishes the management interface set when `IsManagedVRF` is true, applies
management routes, and returns nil (`daemon_apply.go:1628-1733`).

**Trace:** A desired VRF exists with the right table but is down. `LinkSetUp`
fails. Routing records the name managed and returns no error on that branch.
The daemon proceeds to bind tenant/management interfaces, publishes the
management set, and applies routes against the down VRF. Even a different VRF
error returned by the manager is only warned. The commit remains green and no
periodic VRF dirty owner retries; another config apply is required.

**Refutation attempt:** Retaining ownership of a partially created link is
correct, but `managed` is not proof of successful realization. A later commit
may retry but provides neither truthful current success nor bounded recovery.
Linux requires the VRF device up before it can provide the intended forwarding
domain. The caller's nil return independently preserves false success even if
the manager begins returning the error.

**HPC/invariant check:** VRF reconciliation is serialized config-cold netlink
work. Separating ownership from realized/up state and retaining one dirty bit
has no packet cost.

**Why it matters:** Tenant or management traffic can blackhole while the
accepted config and downstream daemon state claim its VRF is available.

**Fix direction:** In routing, retain ownership but aggregate matching-link
setup failure. In the daemon, continue independent binds/cleanup but return a
joined VRF/bind error through the deferred commit result and retain bounded
retry debt if autonomous convergence is required. Test create/adopt setup
failure, management publication, and identical retry.

**Labels:** `bug`, `routing`, `vrf`, `netlink`, `transactional-apply`, `management`

**Dedup note:** Prior interface-reconcile owners cover tunnel/XFRM/bond paths,
not the earlier VRF phase. #5108 owns management-route desired/applied
replacement; #5642 owns rib-group route leakage. Fresh search found no exact
VRF owner.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. The lane caller and direct
`routing/vrf.go` contract are unchanged at the fresh tip.

## Remaining validation gaps

Read-only review precluded adding the missing failure fixtures. Existing tests
do **not** cover:

- Ordinary full-snapshot pre-apply NACK and applied-but-ACK-lost outcomes from
  store promotion through commit return, peer sync, status retry, health, and
  takeover readiness.
- A full-apply failure followed by a successful #5642 partial request, with
  assertions over every snapshot section and applied identity.
- Fail-once route publication and fail-once FIB bump followed by autonomous
  status convergence.
- Multi-feed ready+unready and same-name static+unready bindings through policy
  preflight; current #5645 tests cover only singular/all-unready shapes.
- Injectable stale binding-map clear failure and next-poll retirement.
- A gated session listener proving pair/delete linearizability for v4/v6.
- An in-flight RG reconcile barrier crossing shutdown, including direct VIP
  state and post-clear `rg_active` writes.
- Unreadable/malformed kernel journal across first election and the systemd
  promotion wrapper.
- Packet-facing zoned/unzoned duplicate-address and live unit-0 nft ordering.
- VRF `LinkSetUp`/bind fail-once behavior through the daemon commit result and
  identical autonomous retry.

No privileged hardware/netlink/nft/loss-cluster test was run; package tests are
hermetic and therefore cannot refute these live scheduling and transaction
boundaries.

## Findings

### Z3-F01

**Title:** Separate validation and forwarding ArcSwaps can stamp an old permit with the new generation

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/snapshot_refresh.rs:303-304` stores `shared_validation` and `ha.forwarding` separately. The worker independently loads validation first and forwarding afterward at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/worker/loop_body/mod.rs:364-372`. There is no common bundle identity or reader retry. The flow-cache contract uses the separately loaded validation pair as the decision stamp.

**Trace:** Apply policy generation G+1 that changes an old permit to deny. The coordinator stores validation G+1, a worker observes it while retaining forwarding G, evaluates the old permit, and inserts the result stamped G+1. The coordinator then stores forwarding G+1. The stale permit now compares equal to the current generation and survives the publication window instead of being invalidated.

**Refutation attempt:** Build-before-publish prevents a rejected candidate from rotating either Arc, but it cannot make two successful stores atomic. ArcSwap ordering makes each pointer publication safe, not the pair coherent. Reversing load/store order merely creates a different mixed tuple; no forwarding generation tag exists for a reader-side consistency check. Existing generation mismatch tests do not force this interleaving. The High claim therefore survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** The violated invariant is one immutable worker-visible enforcement generation containing validation, forwarding, and cache authority. A single bundled ArcSwap preserves lock-free reads and one Arc refresh per tick; a seqlock/read-retry alternative must remain bounded and avoid packet-loop spinning.

**Why it matters:** A newly committed deny need not revoke every old permit. The incorrect allow can remain cached after status reports only the new generation, creating a persistent firewall fail-open.

**Fix direction:** Publish a generation-tagged worker runtime bundle containing validation, forwarding, and generation-coupled references through one ArcSwap. Pin one bundle for cache lookup, policy evaluation, and insertion. Add deterministic writer/reader barriers proving only all-old or all-new tuples are observable.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `snapshot`, `generation`, `flow-cache`

**Dedup note:** Exact open owner `#5562`; same root cause, state owner, impact, and single-bundle remediation boundary.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. The stores and worker loads are unchanged at local `origin/master` `fc479ca65`.

### Z3-F02

**Title:** Forwarding arm persists success after discarding mandatory-pin reconciliation failure

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/forwarding.rs:32-44` mutates `forwarding_armed`, propagates it to bindings, discards `reconcile_status_bindings(guard)` with `let _ =`, waits, refreshes status, and requests persistence. In contrast, snapshot apply propagates the same reconciliation error and restores prior state at `userspace-dp/src/server/handlers/snapshot.rs:315-349`. Mandatory XSK/heartbeat/session pin failures return before teardown or publication at `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs:30-114`.

**Trace:** Start with an accepted stored snapshot, fault a mandatory map pin, and issue an arm command. The handler marks the process/bindings armed; reconciliation returns an error before activation; the handler ignores it, waits, refreshes, and persists the armed control state without setting `response.ok=false`. The prior workers/image may remain live while the command is acknowledged as successful.

**Refutation attempt:** The comment argues that no new snapshot is supplied and per-binding `last_error` exposes failure. That does not repair the arm command's own atomicity: its requested transition failed, yet the handler persists and acknowledges the desired state. Pre-teardown abort preserves packet safety for the old generation but makes stale enforcement appear successfully armed. No test injects this error into the forwarding-state handler. The High stale-image/readiness claim survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** Control path only. Propagating `Result`, restoring arm flags on failure, and skipping persistence adds no worker-path cost.

**Why it matters:** Orchestration can treat a stale accepted image as successfully active after mandatory resources prevented reconciliation, defeating readiness and policy-generation authority.

**Fix direction:** Treat arm/disarm as a transaction: save prior arm/binding state, propagate reconciliation failure, restore on error, return `ok=false`, and do not persist. Add a mandatory-pin fault test at this exact handler.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `reconcile`, `readiness`, `persistence`

**Dedup note:** Exact open owner `#5621` (root M06). The issue body names sibling handlers; this forwarding handler is the same discarded-result root and remediation boundary.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. The handler is unchanged at local `origin/master` `fc479ca65`.

### Z3-F03

**Title:** Forwarding becomes visible before its derived CoS owner/lease generation

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `snapshot_refresh.rs:304` publishes new forwarding, while `refresh_cos_owner_worker_map_from_identities()` runs only at `:331`; that routine rotates independently stored owner/live/lease/backlog/vtime maps. No generation or read-retry brackets the set.

**Trace:** A snapshot changes queue/class ownership. A worker observes new forwarding/queue configuration after line 304 but old or missing ownership maps until line 331 and the subsequent map stores, producing transient blackhole, stale-rate, or multiworker over-admission behavior.

**Refutation attempt:** The update window is short and control-thread serialized, but packet workers are concurrent and no barrier waits for them. ArcSwap protects lifetime only; it does not couple map generations. Existing owner-map rebuild tests verify eventual state, not mixed-generation packet behavior.

**HPC/invariant check:** CoS reads must stay lock-free. Bundle derived maps with forwarding, or use a bounded even/odd generation read-retry; do not add packet-path mutexes.

**Why it matters:** A successful commit can transiently violate configured class service and admission guarantees on active traffic.

**Fix direction:** Publish forwarding and every derived CoS authority in one immutable runtime generation, with deterministic mixed-generation tests.

**Labels:** `bug`, `dataplane`, `cos`, `snapshot`, `generation`, `performance`

**Dedup note:** Exact open owner `#5166`.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; unchanged at `fc479ca65`.

### Z3-F04

**Title:** Same-parent unresolved fabric peer replacement republishes the stale old peer

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** `snapshot_refresh.rs:151-155` clones the prior resolved fabrics. At `:267-280`, an empty candidate restores the entire old set and a partial candidate retains old links based only on `parent_ifindex`. `refresh_fabric_links` independently keeps the old set whenever all new rows are unresolved at `:22-67`. The resulting stale row is published to forwarding and HA readers.

**Trace:** Peer A is resolved on parent P. A same-plan commit changes only the peer address to B; B has no resolved MAC. The new build yields no usable B row. Rust restores A because the set is empty, or merges by P, prunes B's unresolved diagnostic because P is present, and republishes A's old IP/MAC. HA redirect traffic continues to A without a bound until B resolves.

**Refutation attempt:** Removing the fabric, changing parent/plan, restarting, or resolving B does close the window. Those are outside the hostile trace: only peer identity changes while P stays constant. Neither preservation path compares desired peer address/overlay identity, and repeated refresh keeps A rather than failing closed. The raw finding is corroborated.

**HPC/invariant check:** Cold, config-bounded work. Comparing stable desired identity before preservation adds no packet-path allocation or lock.

**Why it matters:** Traffic can be misdelivered to a decommissioned/reassigned peer, and the unresolved replacement can be hidden from status.

**Fix direction:** Preserve a resolved fabric only when parent, overlay, and parsed peer identity all match the current desired row. On identity change plus unresolved replacement, remove the old row and retain the skip diagnostic. Add A-to-B unresolved regressions across local forwarding and both HA Arcs.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `fabric`, `ha`, `snapshot`

**Dedup note:** Independently corroborates current raw `A1-b00-F01`. No exact open owner was found; `#5306` owns a different Go cached-snapshot reversion root.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; all Rust and direct producer contracts remain unchanged at `fc479ca65`.

### Z3-F05

**Title:** Flex-only filter rotation compares equal and can leave stale PBR/session semantics

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `FilterTerm` carries `flex_enabled`, `flex_offset`, `flex_length`, `flex_value`, `flex_mask`, and `flex_match_start` at `userspace-dp/src/filter/mod.rs:214-237`. `filter_term_semantics_match` compares neighboring protocol, port, DSCP, TCP, ICMP, action, and modifier fields at `filter/engine/cache_sensitive.rs:287-340` but none of those six flex fields. That comparator drives input-filter semantic rotation detection.

**Trace:** Change only a flex mask/value/offset/start on a PBR term so new packets should choose another routing instance. Old/new filters compare equal; rotation skips the relevant purge/revalidation; established state can retain the old route/zone/NAT path until expiry.

**Refutation attempt:** Flex filters are correctly marked per-packet cache-sensitive for new cache insertion (`filter/mod.rs:265-277`), preventing a direct ordinary flow-cache hit. That does not repair rotation of already established/session-derived routing state whose purge decision uses the incomplete semantic comparator. The focused comparator suite covers constrained flags only and has no flex-only case.

**HPC/invariant check:** Add six scalar comparisons on rotation/cold comparison only. Prefer a derived complete semantic key so future predicate fields cannot be omitted.

**Why it matters:** A committed PBR/security predicate change may not move existing flows to the newly selected forwarding authority.

**Fix direction:** Compare all flex fields or derive equality from a complete match-semantics structure; add each-field rotation tests including routing-instance changes.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `filter`, `pbr`, `cache`

**Dedup note:** Exact open owner `#5293`.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; unchanged at `fc479ca65`.

### Z3-F06

**Title:** Shared three-color policer takes a cross-worker Mutex on every metered packet

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `ThreeColorPolicerRuntime` stores `Mutex<ThreeColorPolicerState>` at `filter/mod.rs:435-440`. Every `meter` locks at `:585-599`; both immediate term evaluation and cached replay call it at `filter/engine/policer.rs:18-47`. The runtime is shared by Arc and poison fails closed to red/drop.

**Trace:** Bind one shared three-color policer to traffic spread across RSS workers. Every matching packet, including cache replay, contends on the same mutex and then updates shared relaxed counters. Under multi-Mpps load, workers serialize and may enter futex contention.

**Refutation attempt:** The no-policer branch is cheap and poison behavior is fail closed, but configured policer traffic necessarily enters the lock. Token state is intentionally shared, so per-worker scheduling does not remove contention. Unit tests prove arithmetic, not multiworker throughput or syscall-free behavior.

**HPC/invariant check:** Direct violation of the no-shared-lock packet-path invariant. Any atomic redesign needs bounded CAS retries, refill clamping, cache-line isolation, and preserved aggregate-rate semantics.

**Why it matters:** A configured rate-control feature can cap forwarding below its own CIR/PIR and amplify tail latency under adversarial matching traffic.

**Fix direction:** Use a cache-line-isolated atomic token-bucket representation or a rigorously bounded sharded design with aggregate compensation; add release disassembly and multiworker contention benchmarks.

**Labels:** `performance`, `dataplane`, `filter`, `policer`, `contention`

**Dedup note:** Exact open owner `#5390`.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; unchanged at `fc479ca65`.

### Z3-F07

**Title:** Per-zone counter folding serializes every active worker once per RX batch

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `ZoneCounterStore` is a shared `Arc<Mutex<FxHashMap<...>>>` at `zone_counters.rs:148-155`. Packet recording is a 64 KiB direct slot LUT plus thread-local arrays at `:269-300`, but each touched batch calls `fold_pending`, takes the global lock, and scans the 63 slots at `:204-227,303-320`.

**Trace:** Active workers accumulate ingress/egress deltas without contention, then every RX batch flush bounces the same mutex/cache line among workers and mutates one hash map. Higher worker count and small batches increase lock frequency.

**Refutation attempt:** The lock is outside the per-packet inner loop and acquired once per touched batch, so this is less severe than F06. It is still in the worker poll loop, globally shared, and active-zone traffic makes it routine. No multiworker benchmark substantiates the comment that it is uncontended.

**HPC/invariant check:** The 2 KiB per-worker accumulator and direct LUT are cache-friendly; the global fold is not. Aggregate per-worker padded blocks from the status/coordinator side or use isolated relaxed atomics.

**Why it matters:** An observability feature can reduce line-rate scalability and increase packet latency across otherwise independent queues.

**Fix direction:** Keep per-worker cumulative slots and aggregate on status reads, preserving clear/exactly-once semantics; add a multiworker batch-rate benchmark.

**Labels:** `performance`, `dataplane`, `zones`, `counters`, `contention`

**Dedup note:** Exact open owner `#5163`.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes; unchanged at `fc479ca65`.

**Title:** Full filter evaluation heap-clones matched string modifiers

### Z3-F10

**Title:** Named-VRF canonicalization and ECMP fanout can allocate during new-flow FIB lookup

**Severity:** Low

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `canonical_route_table` returns owned `format!`/`to_string()` values for named/noncanonical tables at `forwarding/mod.rs:49-74` and is called on packet-driven lookup/recursion at `:1431-1433,1515-1517,2091,2302`. `select_route_next_hop` collects live members into `SmallVec<[&T; 8]>` at `:2772-2787`, spilling for nine or more live candidates; the snapshot wire and builder keep an unbounded `Vec<String>`/`Vec<RouteNextHop>`.

**Trace:** A new flow in a named VRF allocates while canonicalizing the table and at each applicable next-table recursion. A route with at least nine live ECMP members additionally heap-allocates the live-reference spill on every new-flow selection.

**Refutation attempt:** Default tables borrow static strings and ECMP up to eight stays inline, so common configurations avoid both costs. Named VRFs/PBR/route leaks and valid wider ECMP remain live and packet-driven; route recursion is depth-bounded but not allocation-free.

**HPC/invariant check:** Intern tables to compact IDs at build time and use a fixed `[TableId; MAX_NEXT_TABLE_DEPTH]` visited stack. Either enforce an ECMP maximum matching inline capacity or select the Nth live member in bounded two-pass scans without collection.

**Why it matters:** Valid higher-scale routing configurations violate warmed new-flow allocation expectations and expose allocator latency under churn.

**Fix direction:** Apply the interned-table/fixed-stack and no-spill ECMP designs above, with allocation-count tests for named VRF and fanout 9+.

**Labels:** `performance`, `dataplane`, `routing`, `ecmp`, `allocation`

### Z3-F11

**Title:** Addressed empty-zone interfaces enter local delivery while unknown zone 0 admits host services

**Severity:** Low

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** DUP

**Evidence:** `forwarding_build/interfaces.rs:62-92` applies the unknown-zone reject only to nonempty zone names, while configured addresses enter `local_v4/local_v6` independently at `:140-187`. `host_inbound_admits` returns true for a missing zone entry, including id 0, at `forwarding/host_inbound.rs:493-503`. Known zones are correctly inserted with empty/default-deny admission sets at `forwarding_build/zones.rs:90-119`.

**Trace:** An addressed interface with an empty zone receives no `ifindex_to_zone_id`, so its identity resolves to 0; its address is still a local-delivery target. If traffic reaches this Rust classifier under that identity and has no interface override, the missing zone-map entry admits SSH/BGP/etc.

**Refutation attempt:** Current Go AF_XDP bind enumeration normally skips zoneless interfaces; an explicit empty interface override denies; packets arriving on another bound interface carry that real zone. Therefore no clean common-path exploit was confirmed, and severity remains Low defense-in-depth. The Rust state itself is still fail-open for unknown identity and relies on those external gates.

**HPC/invariant check:** A build-time sentinel or reject has no packet cost. Preserve only the explicit global ICMP/ND/PMTUD accepts that precede zone lookup.

**Why it matters:** A future bind/quarantine change can convert a latent identity ambiguity into broad host-service admission.

**Fix direction:** Reject addressed non-lifeline interfaces with empty zone or assign a fail-closed sentinel admission set; add a local-address plus zone-0 SSH/BGP denial test.

### Z3-C01

**Title:** A rejected real forwarding build can destructively prune the live shared zone-counter store

**Severity:** Low

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** COHORT

**Evidence:** Candidate build creates its zone slot map, clones the previous `zone_counter_store`, and immediately calls destructive `reconcile` at `forwarding_build/mod.rs:368-383`. `ZoneCounterStore::Clone` explicitly shares the inner Arc/Mutex and `reconcile` retains in place at `zone_counters.rs:148-155,193-202`. Later filter and CoS compilation can still return `Err` at `forwarding_build/mod.rs:385-403`. Both same-plan refresh and full reconcile pass the live previous forwarding state at `snapshot_refresh.rs:169-181` and `coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs:211-233`. The validation-only path deliberately passes `previous=None` because its comments already identify this mutation at `coordinator/reconcile/snapshot.rs:325-366`; its regression covers only validation at `coordinator/tests.rs:3493-3570`.

**Trace:** Seed cumulative totals for zones A and B. Apply a candidate that removes B but carries a late filter integrity failure (for example, a nonempty missing filter hook) or invalid CoS queue. The real builder clones the live store and prunes B, then returns `Err` from filter/CoS compilation. Refresh/reconcile correctly keeps the prior forwarding state with B configured, but B's cumulative totals are already erased through the shared Arc.

**Refutation attempt:** A failure before line 377 does not mutate, and a successful removal should prune B. Deferred validation is safe because it uses a fresh store. The defect is specifically a real build using `Some(previous)` followed by a later error. Strict Go admission should reject common malformed candidates first, limiting reachability to tolerant/mixed-version/corrupt/internal snapshots; impact is observability rather than packet verdict. Those bounds justify Low/COHORT, but do not refute the mutation. No existing test combines zone removal, a late build failure, and live totals.

**HPC/invariant check:** Cold path only. Deferring prune until all fallible build stages succeed adds no packet-path work and shortens lock hold exposure.

**Why it matters:** A rejected configuration can reset `show security zones`/REST/Prometheus cumulative evidence while the supposedly untouched prior config remains live.

**Fix direction:** Do not mutate the shared store during candidate construction. Build a private candidate view or defer `reconcile` until successful commit/publication; status already filters to configured IDs, so stale entries are harmless until commit. Add same-plan and full-reconcile regressions that preserve B after a late failure and prune it only after success.

**Labels:** `bug`, `observability`, `dataplane`, `snapshot`, `zones`, `counters`, `atomicity`

**Dedup note:** Fresh tip. No exact open/dedup owner was found. `#5171` and the rev-5605 validation regression explicitly cover the validation-only instance; they do not protect real builds that require previous-state carryover. `#5163` owns worker-loop contention, not rejected-build mutation.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. All participating files are unchanged at `fc479ca65`.

## Invariant trace

### Immutable snapshot validation and publication

- Exact snapshot protocol version is rejected before mutation (`server/handlers/snapshot.rs:20-31`); the `(config_generation, fib_generation)` pair is monotone-gated at `:33-107`.
- Policy preflight uses the incoming zone table and scratch counters at `:108-140`. Full reconcile opens mandatory resources and builds complete forwarding before teardown/publication. Same-plan and full handler failures restore snapshot/status and return `ok=false`.
- Candidate builders use typed `SnapshotIntegrityError` for duplicate zone IDs, unknown zone references, malformed addresses, route family/preference, filter references and fields, NPTv6, and CoS bounds. Fresh Z3-C01 is the one shared-store side effect that violates the otherwise immutable candidate contract.
- Successful worker publication is not one transaction: validation/forwarding (Z3-F01), forwarding/CoS maps (Z3-F03), and fabric preservation (Z3-F04) remain exceptions.

### Policy tiers, order, defaults, and host delivery

- Empty default policy is deny and unknown nonempty actions reject the whole snapshot (`policy.rs:1724-1735`). Stable rule and nonzero policy identities are uniqueness checked; policy id 0 remains rolling-compatibility state under existing `#4626`.
- Transit evaluation order is exact zone pair, config-order merge of the two single-wildcard buckets, both-any, scoped global, then default (`policy.rs:2647-2852`). Unknown zone 0 is excluded from every explicit/global tier and reaches the configured default; therefore permit-global cannot admit an unknown identity. An explicitly configured default permit still permits it by design.
- Junos-host order is exact ingress-to-host, from-any-to-host, then host-scoped global (`policy.rs:2975-3069`). No match returns `None` to preserve the documented management lifeline rather than applying an implicit host default deny.
- Every known configured zone receives an admission entry, including empty/default-deny sets (`forwarding_build/zones.rs:90-119`). Global ICMP error/PMTUD/ND accepts precede zone matching. Unknown zone host delivery remains the bounded Z3-F11 exception.

### Address and application expansion

- Address books reject id 0, duplicates, unknown references, wrong-family or malformed prefixes, and unrepresentable sentinels (`policy.rs:1838-1982`). Excluded empty sets fail closed.
- Application terms reject any dropped protocol/port representation and invalid ICMP combinations (`policy.rs:2030-2071,3475-3555`). The matcher indexes exact ports while preserving config-order precedence against ranges and ICMP constraints (`:906-1064`).
- These are representation-integrity backstops, not source-language identity recovery. Once Go has selected the wrong same-name object, discarded duplicate ICMP leaves, or erased a hook, Rust has no tagged provenance with which to reconstruct intent.

### Filter, scheduler, forwarding, and cache authority

- Nonempty missing interface/lo0 filter references reject the whole snapshot; malformed protocol/TCP/ICMP/DSCP/flex/cross-field values also reject. Unknown nonempty terminal filter action compiles to discard.
- Cache-sensitive L4/flex predicates decline ordinary flow-cache insertion, and cached descriptor side effects use inline `SmallVec` storage in common cases. Z3-F05 remains a rotation-comparator omission rather than a matcher omission.
- Route destinations/families/preferences are validated; sorting is longest-prefix then ascending route preference. Next-table recursion has a depth/visited guard and missing targets fail closed. Candidate-level preference is absent on the wire, corroborating A3-b03-F001.
- ForwardingState is immutable per Arc after build, but cache validity and derived CoS authority are split across separate publications. Existing open owners `#5562/#5166` therefore remain the governing atomicity defects.

### Rust/HFT review

- No production `unsafe` block exists in the 40-file lane. The only unsafe blocks are test-only UMEM metadata byte construction in `tests_embedded_poll_filter.rs`; the word in `policy.rs` is prose.
- Bounds are explicit for route recursion, protocol/ICMP bitmaps, flex widths/slices, zone IDs, queue/DSCP fields, and u128 policer refill arithmetic. Saturating arithmetic is used for counters/tokens. No new panic, out-of-bounds, integer-wrap, or lifetime defect survived review.
- Healthy packet paths primarily use immutable maps, stack/value state, thread-local counters, and relaxed telemetry atomics. Known exceptions are the shared policer mutex (Z3-F06), per-batch zone-counter mutex (Z3-F07), full-filter allocations (Z3-F08/F09), and named-VRF/large-ECMP new-flow allocations (Z3-F10).
- The 64 KiB zone-id-to-slot LUT makes record lookup O(1); each worker's four 64-slot u64 arrays are about 2 KiB and local. The global fold loses that locality. UMEM owner-profile telemetry has explicit cache-line-isolation tests.
- Large cold-state clones and module size remain known architectural debt (`#4421`, `#5650`), not new behavioral findings.
