## Material Findings

### F1

**Title:** Composite feed readiness collapses to “any prefix exists,” so deny bindings can publish a partial set

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** The changed manifest contract says an unready feed is omitted and therefore unresolved at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/policies_addrbook.go:145-156`:

```go
// An overlay name that IS present but carries no prefixes still produces a
// (possibly empty) bucket and a nameToID entry, so the policy token routes as a
// book reference to an empty set (match-none). NOTE (#5645): the daemon's
// feeds.Manager.SnapshotForBindings no longer EMITS such a present-but-empty
// entry for an UNREADY feed ... it OMITS the name so the token is unresolved
// and the referencing policy fails CLOSED.
```

The narrow producer contract does not retain per-feed readiness. It skips missing/unready feeds and unions whatever is available at `pkg/feeds/feeds.go:471-481`:

```go
for _, feedName := range binding.FeedNames {
	fs, ok := m.feeds[feedName]
	if !ok {
		continue
	}
	for _, p := range fs.prefixes {
		if _, dup := seen[p]; dup {
```

It then decides readiness only from the aggregate length at `pkg/feeds/feeds.go:484-500`:

```go
sort.Strings(merged)
// #5645: a binding whose feeds ALL lack an installed snapshot resolves to
// no enforceable prefixes.
if len(merged) == 0 {
	continue
}
out[name] = merged
```

That is insufficient in two supported shapes. A binding may aggregate multiple feeds, so one ready sibling makes the name present while another has never succeeded. Separately, the manifest deliberately supports a feed overlay merged with a same-name static book (`feed_enforcement_test.go:264-286`); when the unready feed is omitted, the static name remains in `nameToID` and is representable with only its static prefixes.

Anonymous executable traces on the immutable target confirmed both paths:

```text
PARTIAL-PUBLISH: binding published=true prefixes=[198.51.100.0/24]
while unready-feed hasSnapshot=false

STATIC-ALIAS-PUBLISH: policy remains representable with
bookIDs=[488896378] prefixes=[10.0.0.0/8] and no readiness sentinel
```

**Trace:**

1. Configure address binding `denylist` as the union of `ready-feed` and new `unready-feed`, and reference `denylist` from a deny policy. This is a supported multi-feed binding.
2. `ready-feed` has a last-good prefix while `unready-feed` has never fetched successfully (or was explicitly dropped after its hold interval).
3. `SnapshotForBindings` skips the unready feed, retains the ready feed's prefix, sees `len(merged) > 0`, and publishes `denylist` as resolved.
4. `buildAddressBookTableWithFeeds` gives the partial content a stable book ID. `addrRepresentable` short-circuits on the overlay key, so no `__unsupported_address__` sentinel is emitted.
5. The helper accepts the snapshot. The deny matches only the ready subset; an address that belongs to the unavailable feed is permitted by a later policy/default permit.
6. If the binding name also names a static book, the same under-deny occurs even when every feed is unready: omission leaves the static book resolvable, as the second live trace proved.

**Refutation attempt:** I verified that #5645 correctly closes the exact direct, all-unready, feed-only case; `readFeed` rejects a successful zero-prefix body; #5282 carries a previously ready feed's last-good snapshot; and an omitted pure feed name reaches the policy sentinel. None refutes this finding. `feedState.hasSnapshot` exists, but `SnapshotForBindings` neither requires every referenced feed to be ready nor returns a readiness/taint bit. The configured multi-feed union and static+feed merge are both intentionally supported and tested. The finding therefore survives the High-severity hostile refutation.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is cold apply/fetch publication work. Tracking `allReferencedFeedsReady` while performing the existing bounded feed/prefix walk adds no packet-path allocation, lock, or atomic. The invariant is action-agnostic completeness: a binding must not become representable until every configured constituent has enforceable content (or an explicit operator policy defines partial readiness).

**Why it matters:** A configured deny list can be accepted with only part of its authoritative content, allowing traffic the unavailable constituent was intended to block. The failure can persist indefinitely when one provider never completes its first fetch.

**Fix direction:** Make binding readiness first-class. Require every referenced feed to exist and have an installed snapshot before publishing the binding, or return a separate unresolved/tainted-name set that policy/NAT lowering maps to the unsupported-address sentinel even when static content exists. Preserve last-good data for previously ready feeds, but do not let one ready sibling mask a never-ready sibling. Add multi-feed (ready+unready), same-name static+unready, nested-book, permit, and deny tests through the full snapshot preflight.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `feeds`, `dataplane`

**Dedup note:** Closed #5645 explicitly owns a **direct** feed-bound deny whose feeds all lack a snapshot. F1 requires a different completeness failure: one constituent/static source makes the name representable while another feed is unready. #5646 owns desired/applied callback acknowledgement, and #4925 owns NAT address-set feed expansion; neither owns policy binding readiness. Fresh open-issue searches found no exact root.

**Verified against origin/master:** `origin/master` is `fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`. The manifest files, `pkg/feeds/feeds.go`, and policy representability contracts are byte-identical to target; the executable traces remain valid at tip.

### F2

**Title:** The #5642 route-only repair can mark an old-policy/new-route hybrid snapshot as the new applied config

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** A normal userspace `ApplyConfig` error is recorded but does not abort the daemon's apply pipeline; only required protocol-gate errors return at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:900-909`:

```go
if d.dp != nil {
	var err error
	if applyResult, err = d.dp.ApplyConfig(context.Background(), cfg); err != nil {
		d.recordCompileFailure(err)
		if compileErrorMustAbortApply(err) {
			return commitOverlay, networkdErr, err
		}
	} else {
```

The new #5642 call then runs unconditionally after routing reconciliation (`daemon_apply.go:739-752`). Its manager API clones the previous snapshot, stamps the incoming config, and rebuilds only routes at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go:146-156`:

```go
next := *m.lastSnapshot
nextGeneration := m.generation + 1
next.Generation = nextGeneration
next.FIBGeneration = m.readFIBGeneration()
next.GeneratedAt = time.Now().UTC()
next.Config = cfg
next.Routes, err = buildRouteSnapshots(cfg, next.Interfaces, desiredOverlay)
```

After the partial publish succeeds it records that hybrid as the applied baseline at `manager_overlay.go:179-189`:

```go
m.generation = nextGeneration
m.lastSnapshot = &next
m.rebuildNeighborIndex()
m.rebuildMonitoredIfindexes()
m.publishedSnapshot = next.Generation
m.publishedPlanKey = snapshotBindingPlanKey(&next)
m.markAppliedSnapshotLocked()
```

The anonymous target trace constructed old config C0 with a permit and a live rib-group leak, then called the exact partial publisher with C1 containing a deny after clearing the rule. The wire result was:

```text
HYBRID-PUBLISH: generation=8 embeds new deny config but publishes old
action="permit" with leak-free routes
```

**Trace:**

1. C0 is active: policy P permits a flow and a rib-group leak is present.
2. Commit C1 removes the final rib-group and tightens P to deny. Store promotion already made C1 durable/active before `applyConfigLocked`.
3. The full userspace `apply_snapshot` has a one-shot control response/socket failure. `Manager.Compile` returns before assigning C1 to `m.lastSnapshot`; the helper remains armed on C0. The error is not a required protocol gate, so the daemon continues.
4. Kernel rib-group cleanup succeeds. `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot(C1)` immediately gets a healthy second control request.
5. `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` clones C0, replaces only `Routes`, stamps `Config=C1`, publishes generation 8, and marks it applied. Its policy section still permits; its embedded config says deny.
6. The daemon ultimately reports the original apply error, but C1 remains active/persisted and is eligible for peer sync. More importantly, `publishedSnapshot == lastSnapshot.Generation`, so the one-second status loop has no pending full-snapshot generation to retry. New traffic continues under C0's permit until another complete apply.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked every escape hatch. Errors after a successful full publish already leave C1 in `lastSnapshot`, but an ordinary one-shot `apply_snapshot` failure occurs before that assignment and is explicitly non-aborting. A simple policy/rib-group C1 does not trigger the required-protocol gate. Removing the leak changes route content, so the partial hash cannot duplicate-skip. The partial publisher advances both `publishedSnapshot` and applied bookkeeping, so `syncSnapshotLocked` cannot heal it. The commit error is visible, but visibility does not restore enforcement, and the active config was already promoted. The exact old-permit/new-config hybrid was observed on the live Go publication path, so the High finding survives refutation.

**HPC/invariant check:** Config publication is cold-path work. The violated invariant is atomic generation ownership: every wire section and `Config` pointer in an applied generation must derive from one successfully built candidate. A base-generation/config-identity check is O(1); rebuilding the full candidate uses existing apply-time work and adds nothing to packet processing.

**Why it matters:** A tightening commit can leave the helper accepting traffic under the previous permit while manager bookkeeping identifies the new config generation as applied. That is a live policy-enforcement bypass and suppresses autonomous full-snapshot recovery.

**Fix direction:** Do not run the #5642 partial publisher after a failed full apply. Thread full-apply success/applied generation into `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot`, and make `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` reject a `cfg` whose identity/generation does not match the snapshot it clones. Prefer ordering route-rule reconciliation before a single full snapshot build, or rebuild and publish one complete candidate after the rule change. Add a one-shot full-publish-failure/second-request-success test asserting no hybrid and no applied-generation advance.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `dataplane`, `routing`, `transactionality`

**Dedup note:** #4959 and #5485 concern in-place XDP map/link mutation before failed full publication; #5562 concerns split Rust ArcSwap rotation. Closed #3757 concerns ip-monitoring actuator retry. None owns a successful Go route-only publish that clones old enforcement sections, stamps a new config, and marks the hybrid applied. Closed #5642 introduced this exact call but did not cover prior full-apply failure.

**Verified against origin/master:** `origin/master` `fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53` leaves `daemon_apply.go`, `manager_overlay.go`, and every manifest file unchanged. The target trace reproduces unchanged at tip.

### F3

**Title:** The #5642 zero-leak repair logs and forgets failed route publication or FIB invalidation

**Severity:** Medium

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** The new reconcile helper returns no error and drops publication failure after a warning at `pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:1488-1494`:

```go
published, err := pub.PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot(cfg, overlay, nil)
if err != nil {
	slog.Warn("route-leak snapshot reconcile: routes-only republish failed; the "+
		"userspace FIB may retain a stale inter-VRF leak until the next apply",
		"err", err)
	return
}
```

It likewise drops the required invalidation acknowledgement at `daemon_apply.go:1501-1508`:

```go
// Ordering: bump the FIB generation ONLY after a real publish ...
if _, err := pub.BumpFIBGeneration(); err != nil {
	slog.Warn("route-leak snapshot reconcile: FIB generation bump unconfirmed after "+
		"republish; established flows may re-resolve on a later sweep", "err", err)
}
```

The callee's contract explicitly requires caller-owned retry at `pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_generation.go:46-55`:

```go
// Error contract (#1844): a non-nil error means the helper-side
// invalidation is NOT confirmed ... callers with retry
// semantics (the ip-monitoring actuator's pendingFIBBump) must retry.
// The helperless / no-snapshot early returns are SUCCESS (nil).
```

The anonymous daemon trace observed exactly one publication attempt and no debt, then a publish+bump sequence with the bump error forgotten:

```text
PUBLISH-FAIL-FORGOTTEN: calls=[publish]; reconcile returned with no retry/debt surface
BUMP-FAIL-FORGOTTEN: calls=[publish bump]; reconcile returned with no pendingFIBBump owner
```

**Trace:**

1. C0 has a final rib-group and a corresponding userspace `NextTable` leak.
2. C1 removes it. The initial full apply necessarily builds from the pre-reconcile ip-rule table, so its accepted snapshot still contains the leak.
3. Kernel cleanup deletes the rule. The new routes-only request then has a transient control-socket/helper rejection.
4. `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` logs and returns. No error joins the commit result and no pending route generation is stored; a successful tail lets the commit report success while the helper retains the leak for new flows.
5. There need not be an ip-monitoring transition to invoke its separate retry actuator. The next retry is an unrelated future apply.
6. On the sibling path, route publication succeeds but `BumpFIBGeneration` fails. New flows use the repaired FIB, but established flow/session route caches can keep the deleted inter-VRF decision because this caller does not adopt `pendingFIBBump`.

**Refutation attempt:** `PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot` correctly keeps its internal overlay baseline on failure, but that only makes a later caller retryable; #5642 creates no later caller/debt. The status loop retries only a `lastSnapshot.Generation` not yet published, whereas a failed route publish never advances `lastSnapshot`, and a failed bump follows an already-published generation. The ip-monitoring actuator has retry ownership, but this direct config-apply helper bypasses it. Logging is observability, not convergence. The candidate survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** Both operations are cold and bounded. A single pending generation/desired-route hash retried by the existing one-second status owner adds no packet-path work. The invariant is acknowledgement before success: kernel rule state, helper route state, and flow-cache generation must converge or retain explicit retry debt.

**Why it matters:** A successful final-rib-group removal can leave a stale cross-VRF forwarding instruction active in the live helper, or leave established flows pinned to it, despite the kernel rule and committed config saying the leak is gone.

**Fix direction:** Make `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` return an error into the apply result and persist route-publication/FIB-bump debt keyed by config+route generation. Retry it in the status owner until both publication and invalidation are acknowledged. Do not clear debt on an unrelated partial callback, and add fail-once tests for both stages proving a second poll converges without another commit.

**Labels:** `bug`, `dataplane`, `routing`, `transactionality`

**Dedup note:** Closed #3757 added per-consumer retry to the ip-monitoring actuator; F3 is a new direct #5642 caller that does not use that owner. Closed #3731 concerns netlink rule write errors. Open #4959/#5485 concern different in-place kernel state. No current open issue owns this route/FIB acknowledgement gap.

**Verified against origin/master:** `origin/master` `fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53` has the same void helper and the same caller-required retry contract at the cited lines.

## Cohort Survivor

### C1

**Title:** The user application-set NAT regression guard can pass with a duplicated member and a missing member

**Severity:** Low

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** COHORT

**Evidence:** `pkg/dataplane/userspace/nat_predefined_set_5629_test.go:179-189` checks total length and membership, but never deletes or marks a seen expected pair:

```go
terms := buildSourceNATSnapshots(cfg, nil)[0].MatchApplications
want := map[protoPort]bool{{proto: 6, port: 4444}: true, {proto: 17, port: 5555}: true}
if len(terms) != len(want) {
	t.Fatalf("user application-set expansion changed: got %+v", terms)
}
for _, term := range terms {
	pp := protoPort{proto: term.Protocol, port: term.Ports[0].Low}
	if !want[pp] {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected user-set term %+v", term)
	}
}
```

Two identical `tcp/4444` terms have the expected length and both satisfy `want[pp]`, so the test passes while `udp/5555` is absent. The predefined-set tests above correctly `delete(want, pp)` and assert the map is empty, making this inconsistency concrete.

**Trace:** Not required for COHORT. This is test-only; the current resolver expansion is correct.

**Refutation attempt:** The production `ExpandApplicationSet` deduplicates current output, and the exact predefined bundle tests are strong. That refutes a live production finding. It does not refute the compatibility guard's false-pass: the test claims user-set bit identity but cannot distinguish duplicate substitution.

**HPC/invariant check:** Test-only; no runtime allocation, locking, atomics, bounds, or hot-path effect.

**Why it matters:** A future precedence/expansion regression can remain green while silently dropping one user-set member from SNAT matching.

**Fix direction:** Consume expected keys (`delete`) while rejecting duplicates, assert the expected map is empty after the loop, and guard `len(term.Ports)==1` before indexing. Add the same user-set unchanged guard for DNAT.

**Labels:** `test`, `nat`, `audit`

**Dedup note:** No exact prior root was found. This is test-strength debt and belongs in the campaign cohort, not an individually filed production issue; #4422 is the nearest broad container.

**Verified against origin/master:** The test is byte-identical on `origin/master` `fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`.

## Findings

### D-A7-b00-F01

**Title:** The #5642 routes-only republish is outside the acknowledged full
dataplane apply transaction

**Severity:** High

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** MATERIAL

**Evidence:** The full dataplane call records a generic error but returns from
the phase only for two required-protocol sentinels. Any control-socket timeout,
snapshot-build error, or other non-protocol failure falls through
(`pkg/daemon/daemon_apply.go:900-912`):

```go
if d.dp != nil {
	var err error
	if applyResult, err = d.dp.ApplyConfig(context.Background(), cfg); err != nil {
		d.recordCompileFailure(err)
		if compileErrorMustAbortApply(err) {
			return commitOverlay, networkdErr, err
		}
	} else {
		d.recordCompileSuccess()
	}
}
```

`applyConfigLocked` then always calls `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot` after rule
reconciliation (`daemon_apply.go:754-773`). The partial publisher clones the
manager's *previous* `lastSnapshot`, replaces `Config` and `Routes`, but leaves
policy, NAT, interfaces, feeds, and the other sections from that previous
snapshot (`pkg/dataplane/userspace/manager_overlay.go:146-158`):

```go
next := *m.lastSnapshot
nextGeneration := m.generation + 1
next.Generation = nextGeneration
next.FIBGeneration = m.readFIBGeneration()
next.GeneratedAt = time.Now().UTC()
next.Config = cfg
next.Routes, err = buildRouteSnapshots(cfg, next.Interfaces, desiredOverlay)
if err != nil {
	return false, fmt.Errorf("build route overlay snapshot: %w", err)
}
```

That stale-baseline partial snapshot is sent and promoted as the current
applied snapshot at `manager_overlay.go:169-196`. This is reachable after an
ambiguous full-snapshot timeout: `process_control.go:47-50,103-123` explicitly
documents that Go can report a failed request after the helper has already
applied it, and each request uses a fresh Unix connection.

The new reconciler also converts both of its own load-bearing outcomes into
logs and has no return value (`daemon_apply.go:1488-1508`):

```go
published, err := pub.PublishRouteOverlaySnapshot(cfg, overlay, nil)
if err != nil {
	slog.Warn("route-leak snapshot reconcile: routes-only republish failed; the "+
		"userspace FIB may retain a stale inter-VRF leak until the next apply",
		"err", err)
	return
}
if !published {
	return
}
```

The subsequent generation-bump error is likewise only warned. The tail result
joins networkd, DHCP, nft, IPsec, and interface errors, but no route-republish
outcome (`daemon_apply.go:2085-2092`). In contrast, the existing ip-monitoring
caller of the same APIs returns failure, retains dirty state, and sets
`pendingFIBBump` until a confirmed retry
(`pkg/daemon/daemon_ipmon.go:314-346`).

**Trace:**

1. Generation C1 is live in the AF_XDP helper. It contains an inter-VRF
   rib-group leak and, independently, a policy that C2 will tighten.
2. An operator commits valid C2, removing the final rib-group and tightening
   that policy. `d.dp.ApplyConfig(C2)` sends the full C2 snapshot built from the
   pre-reconcile ip-rule table.
3. The helper applies C2, but the response is lost or exceeds the bounded
   control deadline. Go returns a generic error before assigning C2 to
   `m.lastSnapshot`; `compileErrorMustAbortApply` is false, so the daemon keeps
   running the commit with C1 as the manager baseline.
4. `applyRoutingRules` successfully removes the kernel rib-group rule.
5. `reconcileRouteLeakSnapshot(C2)` opens a second control connection, clones
   the C1 baseline, substitutes C2's config pointer and leak-free routes, and
   successfully applies that partial snapshot. This can overwrite the helper's
   already-applied C2 policy/NAT state with C1 state while recording the hybrid
   as the current published generation.
6. If the second publish instead fails, the pre-reconcile userspace leak simply
   remains. If publish succeeds but `BumpFIBGeneration` fails, new route state
   is present but established sessions can retain cached C1 leak routes; this
   caller sets no pending-bump retry.
7. With otherwise clean tail reconciles, `applyConfigLocked` returns nil and
   `commitAndApply` reports success and may sync C2 to the peer. No autonomous
   full-apply or route-publish retry is armed on the local node. New flows can
   evaluate the replayed C1 policy, and stale established flows can retain the
   removed leak until an unrelated future apply/bump.

**Refutation attempt:** I checked whether the first failure necessarily stops
the helper, whether manager/status reconciliation retains a newer full
snapshot, whether a later phase returns an error anyway, and whether an
existing dirty owner retries. None refutes the trace. `requestDetailedLocked`
uses a new connection per call and can fail on the response after helper-side
application. `manager_compile.go:323-327` updates `lastSnapshot` only after the
full request returns successfully, so the ambiguous timeout leaves C1 as the
partial publisher's baseline. A failed partial publish likewise leaves no new
snapshot for the status loop to replay. The daemon's only generic action is
`recordCompileFailure`; neither it nor the new reconciler creates retry debt or
an apply error. Session invalidation cannot repair the policy replay because
new flows still consult the stale policy. The kernel rule deletion protects
kernel fallback/local routing only; AF_XDP is the sole live transit forwarding
path. The correctly engineered ip-monitoring caller proves these APIs require
explicit dirty and pending-bump ownership. The finding therefore survives.

**HPC/invariant check:** This is serialized, config-cold control work, not a
packet-hot-path cost. The violated invariant is generation atomicity: a
routes-only publish may derive only from a positively acknowledged full
snapshot of the same config generation, and every kernel-rule, snapshot, and
FIB-bump transition must remain owed until acknowledged. Retrying under the
existing `applySem` adds no packet-path allocation, atomics, or lock contention.

**Why it matters:** A routine control-socket timeout during a security-policy
and routing change can end with a successful commit while the sole live AF_XDP
path enforces old permits and/or a removed inter-VRF route leak. This is a
firewall authorization and VRF-isolation failure, not only observability.

**Fix direction:** Prefer eliminating the second publication transaction:
split next-table/rib-group rule reconciliation from FRR/PBR and complete the
load-bearing rule reconcile before building the full userspace snapshot, so
one acknowledged full apply sees final kernel rules. If two phases must remain,
thread an explicit acknowledged full-snapshot generation into the partial API
and refuse a routes-only publish when the full apply returned any error or its
generation is uncertain. Make the route publish return a typed result to
`applyConfigLocked`; join it into the commit outcome, retain route-reconcile
dirty debt, and reuse the ip-monitoring pending-FIB-bump retry under
`applySem`. Add deterministic tests for full-apply-error/no-partial-publish,
applied-but-ACK-lost, partial-publish failure, bump failure followed by a
duplicate publish, and error propagation through `commitAndApply`.

**Labels:** `bug`, `security`, `routing`, `daemon`, `dataplane`,
`transactional-apply`, `vrf`

**Dedup note:** Closed #5642 owns the deterministic `len(RibGroups)>0` skip and
the absence of a normal post-rule snapshot refresh; its no-fault repro is
fixed. Closed #5118 owns per-rule kernel `RuleDel` error aggregation; this trace
assumes the kernel delete succeeds. Closed #3757 owns the ip-monitoring
engine's separate dirty-bit caller and, in fact, contains the retry design this
new caller omits. Open #5669 owns scheduler republish age/fail-closed handling.
Open #4959 owns in-place XDP classifier-map mutation before a rejected full
snapshot. None owns a post-full-apply-error routes-only publish cloned from the
previous full snapshot, or this caller's missing publish/bump result. Fresh
open title/body searches found no exact owner.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. At fresh tip
`fc479ca65e15c28dd0deb942268556fe0df23c53`, all four manifest blobs are
byte-identical to the target. The cited `daemon_apply.go` behavior remains at
lines 900-912, 754-773, 1478-1508, and 2085-2092; the direct manager contracts
remain at `manager_overlay.go:146-196`, `manager_compile.go:323-327`,
`manager_generation.go:46-56,103-119`, and
`process_control.go:47-50,80-143`. Result: still present.

### A7-b02-C01 (corroborated)

**Title:** The new rule-only routing test manager is not safe to `Close`

**Severity:** Low

**Confidence:** High

**Gate verdict:** COHORT

**Evidence:** The new constructor initializes only rule domains and explicitly
leaves all others nil (`pkg/routing/test_seams.go:52-57`):

```go
func NewManagerWithRuleOpsForTest(ops ruleOps) *Manager {
	m := &Manager{}
	m.nextTbl = &nextTableManager{ops: ops}
	m.ribGroup = &ribGroupManager{ops: ops}
	m.pbr = &pbrManager{ops: ops}
	return m
}
```

The public lifecycle method dereferences the omitted tunnel manager before its
netlink-handle nil guard (`pkg/routing/routing.go:83-89`):

```go
func (m *Manager) Close() error {
	m.tunnel.stopAll()
	if m.nlHandle != nil {
		m.nlHandle.Close()
	}
	return nil
}
```

The manifest comments at `test_seams.go:47` claim that `Close` nil-guards the
partial manager, but only `nlHandle` is guarded.

**Trace:** A cross-package test constructs the rule-only manager, naturally
defers `m.Close()`, completes its assertions, and panics in teardown at
`m.tunnel.stopAll()` because `m.tunnel` is nil.

**Refutation attempt:** Production uses `routing.New`, which initializes every
domain, and current daemon tests do not call `Close` on the partial manager.
Therefore the defect is real but test-only and cannot affect appliance
forwarding or daemon availability. That refutes MATERIAL, not the COHORT item.

**HPC/invariant check:** A nil guard is constant-time shutdown/test work and has
no packet-path or control-plane steady-state cost.

**Why it matters:** The exported seam violates normal resource-lifecycle
expectations and can turn future fault-injection tests into teardown panics,
but it has no live production reachability.

**Fix direction:** Nil-guard `m.tunnel` in `Manager.Close` (and preserve the
existing handle guard), or initialize a no-op tunnel owner in every partial
constructor. Add route-only and rule-only construct/use/close tests, and correct
the comments only after the lifecycle contract is true.

**Labels:** `bug`, `test-infrastructure`, `routing`, `panic`, `defensive-api`

**Dedup note:** This is the same current-campaign root already recorded as
A7-b02-C01, not a new individual issue. The delta adds another affected
constructor and leaves the root valid. No exact open issue exists.

**Verified against origin/master:** Yes. `pkg/routing/routing.go` blob
`b033b4e39ad1a75501d44398897b1aa18008074e` is identical at base, target, and
fresh tip. `test_seams.go` target/tip blob
`c1e610f161102de9a0f1d2a27196542745d917f4` contains the rule-only constructor.
